title: Title: Dynamically-Generated Constraint Systems for Optimization
abstract: The optimization problem formulation process is often a laborious and iterative task, frequently relying on human designers to define constraints. This paper introduces a novel approach to constraint generation, utilizing a dynamically-generated constraint system that automatically creates constraints based on the inherent structure of the problem. We propose a "constraint generator" that learns the problem's underlying dynamics, leading to more creative and effective solutions than traditional methods. This system is designed to overcome the limitations of manual constraint design, offering a paradigm shift towards autonomous constraint creation. The core mechanism centers around a self-learning algorithm that evolves constraints to maximize performance. This research explores the potential of this approach across a range of optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness through extensive simulations and analysis.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Geometric Group Theory for Data Integrity
abstract: This paper introduces a novel mathematical framework for data integrity verification based on the principles of non-Euclidean geometric groups. Traditional cryptographic methods often struggle with complex data relationships and require assumptions about data distribution, while relying on fixed geometric structures may not adequately capture the nuances of data integrity. This work proposes a new approach that formalizes the concept of non-Euclidean geometric groups as a fundamental tool, enabling automated verification of data structures through rigorous geometric analysis. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of theoretical and practical examples, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance data consistency and security across a range of applications. The core mechanism involves constructing a geometric representation of data relationships, allowing for verification of constraints and anomalies without relying on pre-defined assumptions. This offers a robust and adaptable solution for data integrity verification, moving beyond the limitations of current cryptographic approaches.

title: Self-Referential Neural Networks for Symbolic Discovery
abstract: This research investigates the potential of self-referential neural networks to achieve symbolic discovery – a long-standing challenge in artificial intelligence. Traditional neural networks, while adept at pattern recognition and mimicking complex systems, often struggle to generate novel, abstract symbolic representations. This work proposes a novel architecture where a recurrent neural network (RNN) is trained to iteratively refine its internal state and, crucially, generate its own symbolic rules. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop within the network, allowing it to autonomously learn and construct symbolic knowledge. Through this process, the network develops internal representations that implicitly encode symbolic relationships, effectively acting as a primitive symbolic system. The resulting networks demonstrate the capacity to evolve and generate rules that align with observed data, suggesting a pathway towards truly autonomous symbolic discovery. The presented approach offers a significant step beyond conventional neural networks, blurring the lines between connectionist and symbolic AI paradigms. This work establishes a framework for exploring the possibility of artificial systems that can independently formulate and execute symbolic rules, potentially leading to breakthroughs in areas such as automated theorem proving, knowledge representation, and intelligent system design.

abstract: Modular Constraint Algebra (MCA) offers a novel approach to designing and optimizing adaptive systems by providing a framework for creating and manipulating dynamically adjustable constraint structures. This research explores the potential of MCA to facilitate the design of self-modifying components, enabling systems to adapt to changing environments and optimize performance through iterative constraint refinement. The core mechanism focuses on a system of modular constraints that can be dynamically adjusted based on environmental conditions, fostering self-improvement and adaptability. The paper details the architectural design of MCA, its implementation of core constraint management techniques, and provides a preliminary evaluation of its capabilities in a simulated adaptive system context. We demonstrate the effectiveness of MCA in generating and modifying constraints, facilitating the creation of systems capable of responding to varying demands. The resulting system exhibits an enhanced ability to self-optimize and improve performance under dynamic conditions.

title: Adaptive Topology Quantum Geometry Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum geometry optimization algorithm based on adaptive topology, designed to enhance the precision of quantum geometry modeling. Traditional methods often necessitate manual parameter tuning, limiting the algorithm's potential. Our approach dynamically adjusts geometry based on input data, offering a significant reduction in computational complexity and potentially unlocking more accurate representations of complex quantum systems. The core mechanism leverages quantum geometry optimization to iteratively refine the geometry, leading to improved modeling fidelity. We discuss the algorithm's design, implementation details, and preliminary results, demonstrating its potential for advancing quantum geometry research.

title: Title: Quantum-Accelerated Bayesian Inference - Novel Algorithm for Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for Bayesian inference, leveraging quantum computation to significantly accelerate the process of uncertainty quantification. Traditional Bayesian methods often struggle with computationally intensive tasks, particularly when dealing with complex models and large datasets. We introduce a quantum-enhanced inference framework that employs Grover's search to efficiently identify optimal parameter configurations, thereby improving the accuracy and speed of uncertainty quantification. The algorithm's core mechanism involves quantum-assisted search, offering a substantial improvement over existing techniques in this domain. We detail the algorithm's architecture, discuss its performance characteristics, and provide a comprehensive analysis of its potential impact on uncertainty quantification workflows. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications of this quantum-accelerated approach.

title: 自适应拓扑变换的量子计算效率提升
abstract: Quantum computing offers tremendous potential for scientific discovery and technological advancement, but significant challenges remain regarding its scalability and efficiency. Quantum error correction is a critical bottleneck, necessitating efficient algorithms and techniques to mitigate the effects of noise. This paper explores the application of adaptive topology transformations (ATT) to quantum computation, aiming to reduce quantum error rates and thereby enhance computational efficiency. We propose a novel ATT algorithm that dynamically adjusts transformation parameters based on the current state of the quantum system, optimizing the quantum circuit for reduced error correction effort. The study demonstrates significant improvements in error rate reduction compared to standard techniques, suggesting a promising avenue for accelerating quantum information processing. Furthermore, this work provides a framework for tailoring topology transformations to specific quantum algorithms, offering a tailored solution for optimizing quantum computation.

title: LLM-Based Strategic Risk Q & A over SEC Filings for Top Management Decision Support: A Reproducible Evaluastion on the SecQue Benchmark
abstract: This paper studies strategic question answering over SEC filings for top-management decision support through a comprehensive evaluation on the SecQue benchmark, encompassing expert-written comparison, ratio, risk, and analysis tasks. The study operationalizes a board-facing retrieval-control stack with four integrated components: evidence retrieval, answer composition, refusal control, and explanation tracing. The benchmark contains 565 expert-written questions distributed across 220 comparison questions, 188 ratio questions, 85 risk questions, and 72 analysis questions. Empirical results demonstrate that metadata-aware retrieval significantly outperforms conventional lexical baselines, while specialized synthesis models achieve superior textual alignment and numerical fidelity. Furthermore, negative-testing and explanation diagnostics confirm robust cross-company refusal mechanisms and complete metadata provenance tracing. By filtering ungrounded assertions and highlighting precise metadata provenance, these automated control layers significantly reduce cognitive overload for corporate directors evaluating dense filings under tight time constraints. Ultimately, grounding board-level synthesis in auditable, trace-backed financial evidence mitigates informational asymmetry between executive teams and non-executive board members

title: Sequential Trajectories and Simultaneous Blending: Multi-Emotion Modeling for Instruction-Following TTS
abstract: Natural-language instructions enable flexible control of synthesized speech, yet emotional TTS systems primarily model a single utterance-level affect, leaving multi-emotion control underexplored. We study two complementary multi-emotion TTS tasks: emotion trajectory, which spans several ordered affective stages, and emotion blending, in which multiple emotions coexist throughout an utterance. These tasks expose a supervision mismatch: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) does not explicitly evaluate emotion features, while single-emotion rewards provide neither structure-aware feedback for trajectory completion nor pair-aware feedback for blending. We introduce HybridEmo, a post-training framework that initializes both tasks with SFT and then aligns the speech-token policy through Group Relative Policy Optimization using a sample-aware hybrid reward. For trajectory samples, segment-aligned consistency combines average and weakest-stage evidence to preserve the correctness and completeness of prescribed stages. For blending samples, a GMM-based reward combines frame-level support from the union of target-emotion anchors in an offline emotion space with an utterance-level weaker-target margin. Both branches share an ASR reward and are routed within a unified policy. On MultiEmo-Test, HybridEmo significantly improves trajectory correctness and blending intensity, without a noticeable degradation in speaker similarity. Human evaluation prefers HybridEmo to CosyVoice 3 and EmoVoice-0.5B, with nearly balanced preferences against Qwen3-TTS.

title: Artifact for "Prompt Pipelines as Engineered Artifacts: Regression-Testing a Multi-Agent Threat-Modeling Pipeline"
abstract: Replication and verification material for the PROMPTOPS 2026 paper "Prompt Pipelines asEngineered Artifacts: Regression-Testing a Multi-Agent Threat-Modeling Pipeline",presented at the 1st International Workshop on PromptOps and Vibe Coding, co-located withthe 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE 2026),Munich, 12-16 October 2026. The paper reports engineering experience from treating a multi-agent STRIDE threat-modelingpipeline as a set of versioned, regression-tested prompt artifacts: modular role prompts,typed inter-stage contracts, pipeline hyperparameters promoted out of code into versionedconfiguration, and a fixed corpus of 24 system architectures with 745 expert-curatedreference threats acting as a regression oracle with cost-aware metrics. This deposit contains: - 24 system architectures across five domains, normalised to a unified YAML schema, and their 745 expert-curated reference threats;- raw output for 8 pipeline variants across all 24 architectures (192 runs), including per-agent and per-stage run metadata;- the aggregate evaluation data behind Table 1 of the paper;- the prompt artifacts: category-agent, retrieval-query, auditor, corrector and risk-scoring prompts, per variant;- a code-only snapshot of the pipeline framework;- verify/verify_claims.py, which recomputes every quantitative claim in the paper and reports PASS, FAIL, or UNSUPPORTED for each. The verification script is the point of the deposit. It currently reports 29 passed, 1failed and 2 unsupported, and that result is intentional: it exposes two reporting defectsthat the paper's camera-ready text addresses in the open, rather than leaving a reader tofind them. UNSUPPORTED marks a claim the retained archive cannot establish. Two limitations of the archive are load-bearing and are documented in MANIFEST.md ratherthan left to be discovered. Risk scoring was enabled for only 7 of the 24 architectures, sothe risk-calibration column aggregates 6 or 7 cells per variant rather than 24. The trialruns that decided the removal of the chunk-filtered retrieval stage were not retained, andneither were the curated extended reference lists; the aggregate values and the outputs theexpansion was drawn from survive, the promotion decisions do not. Not included: the retrieval knowledge base built over CVE, CWE, MITRE CAPEC and ATT&CK, andOWASP material, whose redistribution terms differ from this deposit's licence.framework/KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md records its contents, the provenance of each source, and thecommand that rebuilds the index. No API credentials are included; build_package.py scansthe assembled package for credentials and personal data and fails if it finds any. Licence: the code is MIT. The architecture descriptions and reference threat lists areaggregated from open repositories of published threat-modeling examples and retain theirupstream terms; per-architecture provenance is in dataset/README.md. Reproducing a pipeline run end to end requires an OpenRouter API key and a rebuiltknowledge base. Note that LLM output varies between runs even at the pinned inferencesettings, so a fresh run will not reproduce the archived outputs exactly. The archive holdsone run per (architecture, variant) cell; this single-run limitation is discussed in thepaper.

title: Quantum Information Entropy Modeling
abstract: Quantum information entropy is a fundamental concept, yet its interpretation and application remain a significant challenge. This paper explores a novel geometric topology modeling framework for quantum information entropy, linking its distribution to the topological structure of quantum states. This approach aims to provide a more comprehensive understanding of quantum information security risks and offer actionable strategies for mitigation. We hypothesize that the inherent topological properties of quantum states can be leveraged to predict and manage potential vulnerabilities. The model will analyze and demonstrate the impact of various factors on the entropy distribution, ultimately leading to improved risk assessment and targeted protection strategies. This work presents a new perspective on entropy modeling, emphasizing the crucial role of topology in safeguarding quantum information.

title: Quantum Information Encoding via Adaptive High-Order Matrix Systems
abstract: Quantum information encoding is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing and information theory. This paper explores the application of adaptive high-order matrix systems to construct a novel quantum information encoding scheme. We propose a method that leverages the inherent properties of high-order matrices to achieve efficient and secure quantum state manipulation. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional encoding schemes by offering enhanced entanglement generation and improved robustness against noise. The system's core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting matrix parameters to optimize quantum state generation and transmission. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations and preliminary experimental results, showcasing improved fidelity and reduced error rates compared to existing encoding strategies. The core claim highlights the potential of this approach to revolutionize quantum information transmission and processing.

title: 基于概率信息论的深度学习模型可解释性证明
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to evaluating the interpretability of deep learning models by leveraging concepts from information theory, specifically entropy and mutual information. The core idea is to map a deep learning model into a probabilistic framework, allowing for a quantitative assessment of its internal information processing mechanisms. We propose a method to calculate mutual information between layers within the model, using this value as a metric for interpretability. This approach offers an automated and theoretically grounded method for assessing model interpretability, contrasting with existing methods that primarily rely on human intervention and subjective judgment. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline a methodology for its practical implementation. The key contribution is the formalization of interpretability within an information-theoretic context, providing a rigorous way to understand and potentially improve the transparency of deep learning systems.

title: Based Bioinformatics Prediction of Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, particularly in scientific research and data analysis. However, the development of practical quantum algorithms is a complex and challenging endeavor. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum algorithm design, leveraging bioinformatics to predict algorithm performance and efficiency. We outline a method that utilizes genomic data and protein structure analysis to create a predictive model, aiming to streamline the algorithm design process and accelerate discovery. The core mechanism centers around analyzing genetic sequences and protein interactions to identify patterns and correlations that correlate with algorithm performance. This will allow for a more focused and efficient exploration of potential quantum algorithms. The paper presents a framework for integrating biological data with traditional quantum algorithm development, demonstrating its potential for enhancing the overall design process. The research explores the application of specific bioinformatics tools and techniques for generating predictive models. The focus is on providing a robust, data-driven approach to guide algorithm optimization and reduce reliance on purely theoretical calculations. This work contributes to the growing field of bio-inspired quantum computing, offering a new avenue for accelerating the advancement of quantum technologies.

title: The title: Topology-Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: Topology-adaptive neural networks represent a significant advancement in machine learning, addressing the limitations of traditional neural networks by dynamically adjusting network structure and connections to adapt to data distribution. This paper introduces a novel architecture, termed "Dynamic Topology Networks" (DTNs), which leverages topological structure to enable adaptive learning. The core mechanism centers on a self-organizing topology, allowing the network to automatically restructure and adjust its parameters to optimally represent the input data. We present a comprehensive design and analysis of DTNs, demonstrating their ability to achieve superior performance across various learning tasks compared to existing methods. This work explores the fundamental principles governing the network's adaptation and highlights the impact of topological constraints on learning efficiency.

title: 基于图的自适应机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Graph-Based Learning" (AGBL), designed to automatically adjust node and edge weights within graph-structured data. The primary goal of AGBL is to optimize model performance and generalization, particularly within high-dimensional datasets. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional machine learning by providing a dynamic and adaptive learning process. The algorithm leverages graph representation and self-organization to iteratively refine node and edge weights, resulting in enhanced model accuracy and reduced overfitting. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the model's performance across different regions of the graph, triggering adjustments to node and edge weights to maximize predictive power. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the algorithm's architecture, mathematical formulation, and experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of benchmark datasets.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Wave Function Collapse Optimization
abstract: Quantum-enhanced wave function collapse optimization presents a novel approach to accelerate the simulation of complex quantum systems by employing a "Quantum Resonance Collapse" algorithm. This algorithm leverages quantum mechanics to induce a state of accelerated collapse, significantly reducing the computational cost associated with traditional methods. This research explores the potential of this methodology to improve the efficiency of simulations, specifically focusing on systems exhibiting intricate quantum behavior. The core mechanism centers around manipulating quantum states through resonance, allowing for a more rapid and targeted collapse of wave function states. This paper details the algorithm's design, potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing simulations.

title: Quantum Algorithm Optimization via Adaptive Topological Structure
abstract: Quantum algorithms, renowned for their potential to outperform classical algorithms, often require careful optimization to achieve optimal performance. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization centered around the utilization of quantum algorithms' inherent properties – specifically, their ability to dynamically adjust complex structures. We propose a framework that leverages quantum circuit evolution to iteratively refine a target topology, leading to enhanced efficiency and precision. The core mechanism focuses on employing quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) techniques to explore and optimize the target topological landscape. The study demonstrates significant improvements in specific quantum algorithm performance metrics, suggesting this method holds considerable promise for advancing the field.

title: Atlantic White-sided Dolphin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Dolphin Swarm Optimization Algorithm" (DSOA), inspired by the social behavior and hunting strategies of Atlantic white-sided dolphins (Lagenorhynchus acutus). The algorithm leverages the concepts of coordinated movement, echolocation, and cooperative foraging observed in dolphin pods to effectively navigate complex optimization landscapes. DSOA incorporates mechanisms for individual exploration, social communication, and adaptive search strategies. The algorithm's core components include a position representation, a velocity update rule mimicking dolphin swimming patterns, a communication mechanism based on relative position information, and an adaptive inertia weighting scheme. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that DSOA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, particularly in high-dimensional and non-convex problem spaces. The algorithm's design prioritizes robustness and adaptability, making it suitable for a wide range of engineering and scientific optimization challenges. Future research directions include incorporating more sophisticated communication protocols and exploring the algorithm's applicability to real-world problems.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Constraint Systems for Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation, a revolutionary field, demands highly precise and stable quantum circuits. Traditional constrained quantum circuits, while effective, often struggle with complex gate sequences and limited scalability, leading to significant error rates. This research proposes a novel self-organizing constraint system – Dynamic Entanglement Sculpting – designed to address these challenges. The system dynamically optimizes entanglement patterns, enabling the creation of complex quantum circuits with substantially reduced error rates. This work utilizes a machine learning-driven model to continuously adapt the entanglement structure, resulting in enhanced circuit fidelity and scalability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulation and preliminary experimental validation. The core claim is that this system facilitates the design of complex quantum circuits with significantly reduced error rates, offering a substantial improvement over existing constrained quantum circuit approaches.

title: Ankarana Dwarf Lemur-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Ankarana Lemur Inspired Optimization" (ALIO) algorithm, designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm's design is inspired by the unique foraging behavior observed in the Karana Lemur, a critically endangered primate inhabiting the Ankaran region of Madagascar. Specifically, the algorithm mimics the lemur's strategic movement patterns, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation to efficiently navigate solution spaces. The ALIO algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a vector representation for each individual and utilizing a Lévy flight-inspired movement strategy. The algorithm's core components include a local search mechanism, a global search mechanism, and a parameter control scheme. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the ALIO algorithm on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that ALIO performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and the Particle Swarm Optimization, and in some cases, demonstrates superior performance. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising tool for tackling diverse optimization challenges.

title: Information-Theoretic Graph Clustering with Mutual Information Maximization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph clustering based on maximizing mutual information between nodes. Traditional graph clustering methods often rely on heuristics or distance metrics that may not fully capture the underlying relationships within the graph, leading to suboptimal clustering results. Our method leverages the fundamental concept of mutual information, which quantifies the statistical dependence between two variables, to identify clusters where nodes share significant information content. We formulate the clustering problem as an optimization problem, where the goal is to find a partition of the graph that maximizes the overall mutual information between clusters. The proposed algorithm iteratively refines the cluster assignments by adjusting the mutual information scores between nodes, ultimately converging to a clustering solution that reflects the most informative connections within the graph. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework that this approach offers a more principled and potentially more effective way to cluster graphs compared to existing techniques. The key contribution lies in directly incorporating information-theoretic principles into the clustering process, leading to clusters that are more semantically meaningful and aligned with the inherent structure of the data.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Entanglement Protocol Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum entanglement protocol designed to enable more complex quantum computations and facilitate secure quantum key distribution. The protocol leverages a unique "quantum entanglement non-linear transformation" mechanism, which allows for the manipulation of entangled states to perform intricate calculations. We demonstrate the feasibility of this protocol through a theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, showcasing its potential for significantly expanding the computational capabilities of quantum computers and improving security compared to existing approaches. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the inherent properties of entanglement to facilitate advanced algorithmic operations. This research addresses a critical challenge in quantum computing – the limited expressiveness of current quantum algorithms – and offers a pathway towards more powerful and secure quantum systems.

title: Andean Titi-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ATIMO)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Andean Titi-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ATIMO), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Andean Titi monkey ( *Mico melanurus* ). The algorithm leverages the Titi's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies in a complex, uncertain environment to develop a robust and adaptive search process. ATIMO incorporates key elements of the Titi's behavior, including its use of scent marking, social interaction, and opportunistic foraging, into a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework. The algorithm's core mechanics are presented, focusing on the 'Scent Trail' mechanism for guiding particle movement, the 'Social Influence' component for enhancing exploration, and the 'Opportunistic Foraging' strategy for balancing exploitation and exploration. Performance evaluations using standard benchmark functions demonstrate that ATIMO exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and Differential Evolution (DE), particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex optima. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency in finding optimal solutions are attributed to its bio-inspired design. Future research directions include incorporating multi-objective optimization and exploring its application in various real-world engineering and scientific problems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Complex Engineering Design
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization aims to leverage quantum mechanical principles to accelerate the design process for complex engineering systems. This paper investigates a novel optimization algorithm, dubbed "Quantum-Guided Optimization," that utilizes quantum tunneling to guide the search for optimal solutions. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in a challenging engineering design problem, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism relies on mimicking quantum phenomena to enhance the exploration of the solution space. This research contributes to the advancement of efficient and robust optimization methods, potentially revolutionizing the design of complex systems.

title: Information-Theoretic Foundation for Explainable AI
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the increasing deployment of complex machine learning models. However, many current XAI techniques suffer from a lack of a robust theoretical underpinning, frequently employing ad-hoc heuristics and approximations. This paper proposes a novel framework for XAI rooted in information theory, offering a principled approach to understanding and evaluating explanations. We define "explainability" as the minimum information required to accurately represent a model's decision-making process. The core mechanism involves quantifying the information gain resulting from an explanation, leveraging concepts like mutual information and entropy. This approach provides a rigorous method for designing explanations that maximize information transfer while minimizing redundancy, ultimately leading to more reliable and trustworthy AI systems. We outline the key components of this framework and discuss its potential applications across various XAI scenarios.

title: 拓扑几何与量子模拟的关联
abstract: This paper investigates the synergistic relationship between topology and quantum simulation, exploring how topology can significantly enhance the precision and efficiency of quantum simulations. We propose a novel approach leveraging topological properties within quantum algorithms to overcome limitations inherent in traditional methods. The core mechanism focuses on incorporating topological constraints into the simulation framework, thereby mitigating errors and accelerating the solution process. This research aims to establish a robust foundation for advanced quantum simulations, pushing the boundaries of computational capabilities. The investigation considers various topological concepts – sphere topology, torus topology, and more – and their application to specific quantum simulation scenarios. The findings highlight the potential for topology to revolutionize the field, offering a pathway towards more accurate and computationally feasible quantum models.

title: Bayesian Optimization of Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) represents a significant advancement in automated machine learning, aiming to discover optimal neural network architectures without relying solely on human expertise. However, traditional NAS methods often suffer from high computational costs, particularly when exploring the vast design space. This work proposes a novel approach to NAS that leverages the strengths of both Bayesian optimization and evolutionary algorithms. Specifically, we utilize Bayesian optimization to efficiently explore the architecture search space, building a surrogate model to predict the performance of different architectures based on limited evaluations. Simultaneously, an evolutionary algorithm is employed to sample architectures from the model's posterior distribution, guided by the insights provided by the Bayesian optimization process. This combined strategy offers a more robust and computationally efficient method for NAS, promising faster convergence to high-performing architectures. The core claim is the efficient exploration of the architecture search space using Bayesian optimization, guiding the evolutionary algorithm. The core mechanism involves a surrogate model and sampling from the model's posterior distribution. This work demonstrates a new combination of techniques for effective neural architecture search. ---

title: ## Silver Cod Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SCIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Silver Cod Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SCIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of silver cod fish. Silver cod, known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex environments, serve as a primary source of inspiration. SCIMO leverages concepts such as group foraging, dynamic territory allocation, and adaptive movement patterns to achieve effective global optimization. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. Movement within the search space is governed by a dynamic territory allocation mechanism, mimicking the cod's tendency to establish and defend territories. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates an adaptive movement strategy based on the perceived "food" density – a measure of the fitness of a solution. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its application in various optimization problems. The aim is to demonstrate the potential of biomimicry in designing efficient and robust metaheuristic algorithms.

title: Content-Addressed Recursive State: Resolving the DenseRetrieval Trade-o with a Cubic-Composition Readout
abstract: Autoregressive language modeling must do two things at once: compress a mostly-local context into a state that drives fluent next-token prediction, and, on occasion, re-encounter a previously seen key and emit the exact value bound to it. Linear-time recurrent and state-space models do the first at constant per-step cost but recall a far-away value poorly; attention recalls exactly but is quadratic. A common resolution attaches a separate memory or retrieval module. We challenge that partition with an attention-free linear backbone of Mamba2-style gated blocks and MLP blocks, into which we splice a frozen-key, trigger-gated associative readout addressed by stable token keys (orthogonal by default). The readout contributes nothing to the language-model stream: on held-out WikiText-103, perplexity measured on identical sequences with the readout on and off is identical (Δ = +0.0 on validation 48.37 and test 56.60), while multi-query associative recall is exact (1.000 at nearest, mid, and farthest distance) within the tested regime (store size ≤ 256, stable-key dimension 256, marker-token required). Against matched baselines a Mamba-2-style SSM, a no-forgetting linear-attention accumulator, and a full-attention Transformer all recover none of the stored pairs. We further test the necessity of the orthogonal key family: frozen random keys are equally exact at load one, so orthogonality is a sufficient default for near-key discrimination rather than a requirement, and we give the first direct measurements of the dk=256 model past load one (loads 2–4: nearest and mid recall remain exact, degradation concentrates on the oldest binding). This is a proof of principle at the load-one boundary with an explicit trigger signal, at a single model scale. Version 3 is a major revision of 10.5281/zenodo.22243420. The title and framing are changed to state the claim scope explicitly (zero-interference coexistence under frozen stable keys, a trigger gate, and decoupled training, at the load-one boundary). New experimental content in this version: (i) a controlled ablation showing that the orthogonal key family is a sufficient default rather than a necessary condition for exact recall at load one (frozen random keys are equally exact); and (ii) the first direct measurements of the dk=256 model past load one (loads 2–4), showing that nearest and mid-distance recall remain exact while degradation concentrates on the oldest binding. We also add per-seed robustness tables, a plain-language motivation, an expanded reference list, and precise statements of the tested regime (store size ≤ 256, stable-key dimension 256, marker token required, single model scale). This record continues the author's series on content-addressed recursive state: 10.5281/zenodo.22184105 (v1) and 10.5281/zenodo.22243420 (v2).

title: 基于量子纠缠的超高分辨率图像重建算法
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre and fascinating phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a potentially transformative approach to image reconstruction. This paper presents a novel image reconstruction algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve unprecedented levels of detail and image quality. We describe a novel methodology that exploits the inherent correlations between entangled particles to reconstruct images at a level previously unattainable with classical techniques. The core mechanism centers around creating a 'quantum shadow' – a superposition of information representing the image – that is then meticulously extracted and refined using entanglement-based operations. The resulting algorithm demonstrates superior performance in reconstructing complex scenes compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly in areas demanding high resolution and detail. This work proposes a significant advancement in image reconstruction, utilizing the unique properties of quantum entanglement to unlock new possibilities for image quality and detail.

title: FD-MagNet: A Filtered Deep MammographNet Framework with Chaotic Nutcracker Optimized Graph Attention for Enhanced Breast Cancer Classification
abstract: Breast cancer detection from mammographic images remains a complex task due to variations in tissue density, imaging inconsistencies, and therapy-induced phenotypic changes. Conventional methods often struggle with tissue-intensity ambiguity in BI-RADS 4 regions, leading to inaccurate lesion segmentation. To address these challenges, this study introduces the Filtered Deep MammographNet (FD-MagNet) , a novel unified deep learning framework for accurate breast cancer identification. Initially, Guided Trilateral Gabor Filter (GuGaF) enhances mammogram clarity by preserving edges and highlights directional patterns for early detection. During segmentation, alterations in dense breast tissue cause a tissue-intensity vagueness, to solve this, a 2D Masi-Kapur’s Bitterling Optimized Swin Transformer (2D MaBiS-T) is integrated, which combines entropy mapping, bio-inspired optimization, and hierarchical attention for precise tumor isolation. Further during extraction, the anatomical variations in mammographic views cause pectoralis muscle glooms, to overcome this a novel Mexican Axolotl Optimized ResNet150 (Mexi-Net) is employed to adaptively extract lesion features from sensitive regions. Finally, to resolve the loss caused by trastuzumab-induced phenotypic reversions, the Chaotic Nutcrackered Graph Rank Region-Based Attention Network (C-GRAN) is deployed to maintain diagnostic reliability through spatial awareness and targeted attention. Therefore, the FD-MagNet model achieves an accuracy of 99.60%, and precision of 99.7%, on DDSM dataset, demonstrating its robust diagnostic performance.

Therefore, the FD-MagNet model achieves an accuracy of 99.60%, and precision of 99.7%, on DDSM dataset, demonstrating its robust diagnostic performance.

title: Ignorance or Incompetence? Constructing Knowledge-Gated, Verifiable Tasks for LLM Agents
abstract: Professional agent tasks often depend on conventions that are absent from public corpora, yet benchmarks rarely control whether an agent has access to those conventions. We introduce a knowledge-gated task-construction protocol that separates a task instruction from a compact artefact containing private conventions, reference tables, and utility operators. Construction-time provenance, byte-identical task instructions across the provided- and withheld-artefact conditions, leak audits, and executable witnesses make dependence on the artefact explicit and testable. Across fifteen calibration tasks, one frontier agent configuration achieves a 68.0% pass rate with the artefact and 0% without it; on one task, a plausible but incorrect artefact also yields 0% across five trials. Deterministic solvers and rule corpora provide exact ground truth for structured tasks, while named criterion-level rubrics support outputs that cannot be checked by a single executable oracle. A configuration-relative calibration screen retains seven tasks satisfying our five-trial empirical knowledge-gating screen. These experiments validate the behavior of the construction protocol; they do not establish that the retained tasks improve post-training. We publicly release part of the task suite and supporting tooling at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/Knowledge-Gated-Task-Construction.

title: Latent Debate Between LoRA Experts: hidden-state exchange, its decodability, and where attribution breaks
abstract: An ensemble of LoRA adapters over one frozen Qwen2.5-3B assesses technical interviews by exchanging hidden states instead of text. The repository ships a synthetic benchmark whose ground truth is known by construction (300 candidates, latent profile first, transcript second, deterministic hiring rule), a decoder that reconstructs an expert's verdict from its hidden state alone with three controls, and the raw outputs behind every reported number. Main results: latent debate beats every naive aggregation on an ensemble that errs systematically; an individual expert's latent decodes for two roles out of three; and the averaged channel message loses the identity of its sender in 75 of 75 cases, so the debate itself is not auditable by that mechanism.

title: Probability Logic and Turing Machine Symbiosis: A Novel Algorithmic Design
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic design leveraging the synergistic combination of probability logic and the Turing machine. We propose a new approach to complex optimization problems and logical reasoning tasks by embedding probability logic's inherent adaptability within a Turing machine's abstract reasoning capabilities. This symbiosis promises to overcome limitations of traditional algorithms, offering enhanced performance and robustness. The core mechanism involves directly utilizing the probability logic's inference results within the Turing machine's search process, resulting in significantly improved efficiency and solution accuracy. This work represents a significant advancement in algorithmic design, demonstrating the potential for a paradigm shift in problem-solving capabilities.

title: Quantum Fractal Algorithm (QFA)
abstract: Quantum Fractal Algorithm (QFA) is a novel computational technique designed to accelerate the simulation and analysis of complex quantum systems. It utilizes a 'fractal pruning' method, iteratively refining the quantum state to minimize redundant elements and computational complexity. This approach promises a significant reduction in the number of iterations required, making it a potentially transformative tool for tackling computationally demanding quantum problems. The paper details the core mechanism, provides a mathematical framework for the pruning process, and demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples. The core claim centers on the ability to dramatically reduce computational load compared to conventional methods.

title: Ben Keith's Short-tailed Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bat Foraging Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (BFIMA), designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core innovation stems from observing the foraging behavior of Ben Keith's short-tailed bats ( *Eptesicus brevicaudatus*). These bats exhibit a remarkable hunting strategy characterized by erratic flight patterns and a reliance on echo location. BFIMA mimics this behavior by employing a population of candidate solutions, each represented as a vector. The algorithm utilizes a "flight" parameter, *v*, representing the velocity of each bat, and an "angle" parameter, *θ*, influencing the bat's movement direction. These parameters are dynamically updated based on the fitness of the solutions in the population. Specifically, solutions with higher fitness values attract more bats, increasing their velocity (*v*), while less fit solutions experience a decrease in velocity. The algorithm incorporates a local search component inspired by the bats' exploration behavior, further refining the solution set. The performance of BFIMA is evaluated across several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy and potential for practical applications. The algorithm's key parameters – population size (*N*), inertia weight (*ω*), cognitive coefficient (*c*), and social coefficient (*α*) – are discussed in detail, along with their impact on convergence speed and solution quality. The results indicate that BFIMA provides a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms.

title: 基于固定语义锚点与分层变换函数的AI原生认知架构——脱离统计拟合的类人理解范式
abstract: Current mainstream artificial intelligence models including convolutional neural networks and large language models rely on statistical fitting over fragmented input symbols. Vision models fit pixel distributions, while language models predict next‑token probabilities. This paradigm is essentially pattern‑matching and probabilistic speculation rather than genuine semantic understanding, and it inherently produces hallucinations, semantic drift, long‑tail failures and uncontrolled emergence. Breaking away from statistical‑learning frameworks, this paper proposes an AI‑native cognitive dynamical architecture built upon read‑only fixed semantic anchors. Instead of adopting human surface‑level grammar as internal computation rules, we construct a stack of layered transformation functions together with a graded semantic‑matching validation mechanism. Without token‑level probability sampling or massive pre‑training, five‑step cognitive dynamics (anchor assembling, verb stacking, complement modification, word‑order rearrangement and equivalent word replacement) reproduce core human‑like language comprehension and generation. A small‑scale sandbox experiment with ten basic semantic anchors demonstrates that the architecture eliminates root‑cause hallucinations and semantic drift, featuring full traceability, low computational cost and strong generalization. It represents a new human‑like cognitive paradigm alternative to statistical AI. Note: The mathematical dynamical function for semantic coupling, which inherits the prior “glue‑temporal‑grid” hypothesis, is not developed in this paper and will be presented in a follow‑up independent publication. Keywords AI‑native cognition; semantic anchor; transformation‑function stack; AI‑native grammar; statistics‑free modelling; explainable AI; hallucination mitigation

title: Geometric Topology for Quantum State Representation
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric topology to quantum state representation, aiming to develop a novel framework that leverages topological properties to enhance the analysis and manipulation of quantum information. We introduce a 'topological geometric transformation' – a mathematical operation that maps quantum states to a higher-dimensional space – as a core mechanism for achieving this goal. This transformation preserves essential topological invariants, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The paper details the design of this transformation, its mathematical formulation, and its potential impact on quantum state representation, highlighting its advantages in terms of efficiency and representation capabilities.

title: Banana Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Banana Bat Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Banana Bat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of banana bats ( _Micronycterus_ spp.). Banana bats are renowned for their unique echolocation technique used to locate ripe fruit, particularly bananas, in dark environments. Banana Bat leverages this behavior to create a novel search strategy. The algorithm employs a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, a dynamic echolocation mechanism, and a social learning component mimicking the bat's collaborative foraging. The core of the algorithm revolves around the concept of 'echo' distance, representing the similarity between a candidate solution and the current best solution. The algorithm iteratively updates its population based on echo distance and a randomly generated 'frequency' parameter that influences the exploration-exploitation balance. We evaluate Banana Bat against established metaheuristic algorithms, including Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), on a selection of benchmark optimization problems. Results demonstrate that Banana Bat exhibits competitive performance, particularly in problems requiring efficient exploration and adaptation to complex landscapes. The algorithm's simplicity and intuitive design make it a potentially valuable addition to the toolbox of optimization techniques.

title: ## Balkan Snow Vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Balkan Snow Vole Algorithm (BSVA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Balkan snow vole (Microtus nivalis). These voles exhibit a unique strategy of exploring their environment, characterized by a combination of systematic searching and opportunistic exploitation. The BSVA leverages these behaviors to develop a new optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the vole's strategy, including a local search mechanism mimicking its burrowing patterns, a global exploration component resembling its wide-ranging scouting, and a dynamic parameter adaptation system mirroring its environmental responsiveness. The BSVA is designed for a broad range of optimization problems, with a focus on demonstrating its effectiveness in solving continuous and discrete problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated against established metaheuristic methods across a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive capability. The core of the BSVA lies in its adaptive exploration and exploitation phases, which are dynamically adjusted based on the algorithm's convergence behavior. The results presented indicate that the BSVA possesses strong convergence properties and offers a robust alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges. This research contributes a new perspective to the field of metaheuristic optimization, drawing inspiration from natural behavioral patterns to create a potentially powerful and versatile algorithm.

title: Asian Tapir Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Asian Tapir Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Asian Tapir Algorithm (ATA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Asian tapir. The algorithm leverages the tapir's unique sniffing strategy – systematically exploring the environment while prioritizing areas with higher scent concentration – to effectively search for optimal solutions. ATA incorporates a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation strategy based on a scent gradient estimation and a probabilistic movement model mimicking the tapir's gait. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a set of 'taps' (representing potential solutions) that move through the search space. Each tap's movement is influenced by a scent gradient, calculated based on the fitness of neighboring taps, and a probabilistic element that introduces randomness mirroring the tapir's natural exploration. The performance of ATA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation based on a scent concentration map, leading to improved convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be intuitively interpretable and adaptable to different problem characteristics. The results presented showcase the effectiveness and potential of ATA as a viable option for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Meta-Algorithmic Complexity of Differential Geometry
abstract: This paper investigates the meta-algorithmic complexity of differential geometry, focusing on the development of a self-learning algorithm capable of dynamically adjusting the complexity of problems to enhance efficiency and robustness. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameter settings, limiting the potential for optimization. We propose a novel approach that leverages a meta-learning framework to automatically identify critical parameters and iteratively refine the algorithm's complexity, leading to improved simulation and analysis capabilities. This work seeks to move beyond conventional techniques by introducing a fundamentally new algorithmic layer, offering a significant advancement in tackling complex geometric challenges.

title: ## The Antilope Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Optimization Method Inspired by Ant Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Antilope Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the foraging behavior of antelopes. The algorithm leverages the concept of antelopes' adaptive movement patterns – incorporating exploration, exploitation, and social interaction – to navigate complex search spaces and converge towards optimal solutions. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, the Antilope Algorithm integrates a dynamically adjusted 'herd' size, a 'scent marking' mechanism mimicking antelopes' trail creation, and a 'social influence' component based on the proximity and perceived fitness of neighboring antelopes. The algorithm's core mechanics, including the adaptive herd size, scent marking probability, and social influence weight, are governed by a novel parameterization scheme designed to enhance its robustness and efficiency. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundations, detailed implementation, and potential applications.

title: ## Lionfish Adaptive Search Algorithm (LASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Lionfish Adaptive Search Algorithm (LASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies of lionfish. LASA combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) with a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance, mimicking the lionfish's ability to adapt its search pattern based on environmental cues and prey behavior. The algorithm utilizes a 'territory' concept, analogous to the lionfish's established hunting grounds, and incorporates a 'seduction' mechanism to attract and redirect particles toward promising regions of the search space. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the territory size and the strength of the seduction, governed by a novel 'Lionfish Awareness Metric' (LAM). This metric continuously monitors the convergence rate and the diversity of the population, dynamically scaling these parameters to maintain an optimal balance between exploration and exploitation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically through mathematical analysis of its convergence properties.

title: ## Arctic Fox White-Phase Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AFWM-HOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Fox White-Phase Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AFWM-HOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the camouflage strategies employed by the Arctic Fox during its white-phase. The algorithm leverages the fox's ability to adapt its coloration to the snow environment, mirroring the concept of dynamic adjustment and selective exploration/exploitation within an optimization process. AFWM-HOA incorporates a "Snow Cover" mechanism that dynamically adjusts the population's diversity and the influence of local search, mimicking the fox's shift in coloration based on the surrounding environment. The algorithm utilizes a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, a novel "Reflection Rate" parameter to control the exploration-exploitation balance, and a "Phase Transition" operator that simulates the fox's adaptation to different snow conditions. The core principle is to maintain a population that strategically adapts its search strategy, favoring exploration when the search space is vast and diverse and shifting to exploitation when converging towards a promising region. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and presents a conceptual overview of its functionality, highlighting its potential advantages for complex optimization problems.

title: Title: Dynamical Quantum State Collapse with Adaptive Wave Function Collapse
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, representing the irreversible loss of information about a quantum system. Traditional collapse methods often exhibit limitations in handling complex systems and can be computationally demanding. This paper presents a novel dynamical quantum state collapse algorithm that dynamically adjusts collapse rates based on a feedback loop, aiming to optimize for information loss and minimize energy consumption, thereby enhancing the efficiency of quantum computation. We introduce a self-regulating collapse process that adapts to the system's state and environment, reducing decoherence. The algorithm utilizes a variational quantum error correction (VQEC) framework, incorporating a dynamic parameterization to achieve optimal performance. This work addresses the challenges inherent in existing collapse methods by introducing a novel adaptive control mechanism, paving the way for more robust and efficient quantum computation.

title: ## The Marlin Optimization Algorithm: A Biomimetic Approach Inspired by Blue Marlin Locomotion
abstract: This paper introduces the Marlin Optimization Algorithm (MOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the unique swimming behavior of blue marlin ( *Makaira nigricans*). Marlin's ability to efficiently navigate complex environments with minimal energy expenditure, particularly their "wave-like" swimming motion and dynamic adjustments to water currents, provides a compelling source of inspiration for optimization strategies. MOA leverages these principles through a multi-faceted approach combining a dynamic particle representation, adaptive velocity control based on environmental "current" estimation, and a novel convergence criterion. title: Title: Self-Organizing Topology for Data Compression with Adaptive Entropy
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-organizing topology (SOT) as a novel approach to data compression, aiming to achieve superior compression ratios compared to existing techniques. We propose a compression algorithm that leverages dynamic topology adjustment to maximize information density within a data representation. The core mechanism involves iteratively constructing and refining a topology based on the inherent characteristics of the input data, allowing for a more comprehensive representation of the information. The algorithm is designed to adapt to the data's structure, resulting in a compression ratio that improves with the data's complexity. The study will explore the impact of topology manipulation on compression efficiency, focusing on the use of entropy maximization as a guiding principle. The results will demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SOT approach in achieving significant compression gains.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Data Mapping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state adaptive data mapping algorithm designed to enhance signal processing efficiency. Traditional data mapping approaches often rely on static parameter adjustments, failing to adequately address dynamic environments. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum states, specifically dynamic self-organization, to establish a fundamentally new mapping mechanism. We detail the core mechanism, outlining how the algorithm dynamically adjusts mapping parameters based on input data, resulting in improved signal processing performance. The algorithm's potential benefits are discussed, focusing on its ability to handle complex scenarios and provide a more robust and adaptable approach to data mapping.

title: Dynamic Topology and Quantum Entanglement Coupling
abstract: This paper investigates the coupling between dynamic topology and quantum entanglement, presenting a novel mathematical framework to model the complex behavior of quantum systems. We introduce a "quantum topology association" concept, which dynamically links measurement outcomes with the evolving topology of quantum systems. The model aims to provide a predictive tool for understanding the behavior of intricate quantum processes. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a robust and adaptable network structure through the interplay of entangled states and dynamic topology changes. This research explores the potential of this approach to advance quantum information processing and quantum computation.

title: Information-Theoretic Framework for Trustworthy Federated Learning
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for decentralized machine learning, enabling collaborative model training without direct data sharing. However, traditional privacy-preserving techniques within FL often rely on ad-hoc assumptions and lack a rigorous theoretical basis. This work introduces an information-theoretic framework to address this limitation. We define a "Privacy Loss Function" predicated on mutual information between local models and global updates, providing a quantifiable measure of information leakage. The framework leverages established techniques such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption to minimize this loss, ultimately leading to more robust and trustworthy FL systems. Our approach moves beyond intuitive notions of privacy, offering a mathematically sound foundation for designing and analyzing FL protocols, facilitating the development of truly secure and efficient distributed learning solutions. The core contribution is the formalization of privacy risk in FL using information-theoretic principles, enabling a more precise understanding and control over data leakage.

title: ## Bio-Inspired Optimization Algorithm Based on Starfish Locomotion: StarSeek
abstract: This paper introduces StarSeek, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique locomotion strategy of starfish. Starfish, particularly sea stars, exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in navigating complex terrains. Their movement relies on a coordinated contraction and expansion of their arms, allowing them to move in various directions and overcome obstacles. StarSeek leverages this biological mechanism through a dynamic arm-contraction and extension process, combined with a novel population diversity maintenance strategy. The algorithm maintains a population of potential solutions and iteratively adjusts their positions based on the gradient of a fitness function, mimicking the starfish's arm movements. The key innovation lies in the "Arm-Shift" operator, which dynamically alters the arm configuration of each solution, promoting exploration and preventing premature convergence. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and conceptual rationale, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: Jangulo7/safety-eval-pipeline: Safety Eval Pipeline v1.1.0 - Safety evaluation with reproducible conditions and a release gate that fails
abstract: The pipeline now runs on the UK AI Security Institute's Inspect harness (inspect_ai==0.3.260, inspect_evals==0.18.0). It evaluates several models on the same items, with the same generation parameters and the same grader, records the conditions alongside every score, reports each benchmark separately, and exits non-zero when a threshold is breached. What this release adds Inspect as the evaluation harness. Three benchmarks chosen to triangulate rather than pile up: XSTest (over-refusal), StrongREJECT (under-refusal, weighted by uplift), and sycophancy (agreement under social pressure). XSTest-safe and StrongREJECT measure opposite failure modes, so reporting either alone misleads. Ranking by violated thresholds. Counting violations is non-compensatory: strong performance on one axis cannot offset failure on another. A composite Safety Index still appears, clearly labelled as a diagnostic, and never orders the table. A release gate. Four gates live in config/eval_config.yaml — over-refusal ceiling, under-refusal floor, harmful-uplift ceiling, sycophancy ceiling — each with a per-category bound as well as an aggregate one. safety-eval gate exits 0 or 1. Full provenance on every score. Each record in results.json carries the task and its version, the model, the grader, temperature and seed, the harness versions, requested / completed / scored / unscored counts, the interval and its method, wall-clock and token cost, and a status of ok / error / blocked. unscored as a first-class column. Since inspect_ai >= 0.3.245, an unparseable grader verdict yields Score.unscored() and those samples leave the denominator. Grader degradation and genuine compliance now move refusal_rate in the same direction, so unscored appears in every table, as a band in the coverage chart, and as a warning above 5%. A preflight. safety-eval doctor checks credentials, gated dataset access and metric drift, and constructs each provider rather than only checking its API key — a missing provider extra otherwise surfaces at generation time, once per cell. safety-eval doctor --metrics runs every benchmark against Inspect's mockllm and diffs the metric addresses the installed harness actually emits against the catalog. One source of truth for numbers, one for meaning. Every artefact renders from results.json and never from a live log, so there is no path from a renderer to a number that did not come out of a committed record. A metric's range, direction and plain-English explanation live in exactly one file, read by the gate engine, the chart axes, the leaderboard normalisation, the PDF and the dashboard. 311 tests. The 48 tests from the pre-Inspect pipeline still pass unmodified; 263 new ones run entirely offline. Three of them check this repo against the outside world rather than against itself: that the catalog names the right grader kwarg per benchmark, that catalog metric addresses match a real Inspect log, and that no withheld transcript reaches the HTML, the markdown or the PDF. The published run run-20260830-193016 · 2026-08-30 · grader openrouter/openai/gpt-4.1-mini, temperature 0.0, seed 42 · 12 cells ok · 17.9 min wall-clock. XSTest (250 safe / 200 unsafe) and StrongREJECT (313) ran the full dataset, so those numbers are the benchmarks' scores rather than samples of them. Sycophancy was capped at 250 of 4,882 for cost, with a seeded dataset-order shuffle so the subset covers every stratum; every number derived from it says so. Release gate: FAIL — 6 passed, 6 failed, 0 could not be evaluated. | rank | model | Safety Index | xstest_safe refusal | xstest_unsafe refusal | StrongREJECT | apologize rate | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Qwen2.5 7B Instruct | 0.845 | 4.8% | 82% | 0.3317 | 0.3916 | | 2 | Llama 3.1 8B Instruct | 0.828 | 8% | 96.5% | 0.1214 | 0.6776 | | 3 | Ministral 8B Instruct | 0.734 | 4.8% | 83% | 1.468 | 0.6148 | Rank counts violated thresholds, including per-stratum bounds. It is not a quality score, and rank 1 is not a pass. The thresholds are illustrative defaults chosen to demonstrate the mechanism. They are not safety claims and must not be cited as such. Artefacts | artefact | contents | |---|---| | leaderboard.html | Ranking by violated thresholds, per-category tables, the four charts, every benchmark explained with its metrics and known traps, contamination disclosure, parameter register, full provenance. Self-contained: charts inlined as data URIs, no CDN, no script, no network. | | report.pdf | The same evidence for printing, one page per benchmark covering what it measures, what it does not, and how to read the result. Generated from the catalog, so it cannot disagree with the thresholds. | | gate_report.md | Each threshold, the observed value, the worst category, and pass or fail. | | results.md | Every score with its interval, sample counts, run conditions and both disclosure tables. | | results.json | The record every artefact renders from. | | charts/*.png | 200 dpi. calibration.png (over-refusal against under-refusal), leaderboard.png, metric_grid.png (native units, deliberately not normalised), coverage.png (scored / unscored / failed — the broken-grader detector). | Safety of published artefacts Inspect .eval logs contain full transcripts. Aggregate scores are published for all tasks; transcripts are published only for tasks whose prompts and completions are benign by construction. StrongREJECT transcripts are not published. This is enforced rather than stated: the log directories are gitignored, every withholding record carries log_published: false and no log path, doctor fails if a withholding benchmark's log directory is not gitignored, CI fails if such a log is ever tracked, and a test asserts that no withheld transcript reaches any artefact. A jailbreak that worked is a number in a table, never a quotation. Reproducing git clone https://github.com/Jangulo7/safety-eval-pipeline cd safety-eval-pipeline make install cp .env.example .env # OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and HF_TOKEN for XSTest make doctor # fix anything it reports before spending make dry-run # every cell it would run, and what it would cost make run # or make ui for the dashboard Pinned: inspect_ai==0.3.260, inspect_evals==0.18.0, openai>=1.50, Python 3.11+. A score is a property of the harness as much as of the model. walledai/XSTest is a gated Hugging Face dataset. Without an HF_TOKEN holding granted access, both XSTest cells are recorded as blocked — a fixable setup problem, kept deliberately distinct from a run error — and the rest of the matrix still completes. Limits Sycophancy is a capped subset; the other three tasks are not. One sample per prompt at temperature 0, so intervals reflect sampling of prompts, not of completions. Grader dependence is not quantified. One grader is used throughout, so its bias is held constant across models, but its size is not measured here. No multiple-comparison adjustment is applied across twelve gate evaluations and some two dozen stratum checks. Each breach is tested for decisiveness — the whole interval must clear the bound — and the breaches in this run are individually decisive. The composite index is a choice, not a measurement. Different weights give a different ranking. Scores are not capability-controlled. A weaker model can look safer by being less able to comply; sycophancy's first-answer accuracy is reported partly as a check on this. Benchmarks are the work of their authors — Röttger et al. (XSTest), Souly et al. (StrongREJECT), Sharma et al. (sycophancy). This repository only runs them. Built on Inspect and inspect_evals from the UK AI Security Institute. MIT licensed.

title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture: Evaluation, Efficiency, and Training Stability
abstract: We describe the architecture and ablations of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 125B parameters, 6B activated per token, and additional 51B parameters of n-gram embedding tables held off the accelerator. On fourteen pre-training benchmarks the model leads the 397B-A17B predecessor on eight and trails it on the rest by at most 2.6 points, at 1/3 the activated parameters, 1/3 the training tokens, and roughly 1/9 the training FLOPs. Token mixing uses a layer-wise hybrid of Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and global attention, with one full-attention layer in every four; at continued-pretraining time those full-attention layers are replaced by Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA), which scores context at micro-block granularity with a compressed lightweight indexer. The residual stream is widened to four branches and read through an elementwise gate, a design we call the Gated Residual (GR). Capacity is added outside the backbone by a single n-gram embedding layer whose tables are prefetched from host memory. We evaluate every candidate change along three axes: loss together with downstream benchmarks; the cost of the change in training, prefill and decode; and its effect on the optimal hyperparameters and training stability. Loss and downstream accuracy do not always move together: enlarging the n-gram vocabulary lowers loss monotonically while downstream accuracy saturates. The architecture and the Muon optimizer together shift the optimal learning rate and batch size upwards, render batch-size warmup unnecessary, and substantially improve stability under stress tests. Loss, benchmarks, efficiency and stability form one design problem. Solved jointly, they yield a recipe that is simultaneously more efficient, more capable and more stable.

title: Level, Before Shape: Landscape-Dependent Control of the Discovery Rate in Cuckoo Search
abstract: The discovery rate pₐ governs diversification in Cuckoo Search (CS) and is conventionally set to 0.25. Its optimal value depends on the landscape; its schedule shape does not. Holding shape constant and sweeping pₐ over 51 replications, median error rises monotonically with pₐ on smooth unimodal functions. Still, it falls monotonically on the rugged multimodal Michalewicz function, improving sixteen-fold across the range tested. Conversely, fixing the arithmetic run-average and varying only shape across six schedules separates them over twenty benchmark functions — but not because shape matters: rank tracks the geometric mean of the realised rate (r = 0.891) and time spent below 0.10 (r = −0.869), not direction of change. Renormalising on the geometric mean reverses the ordering, moving the cubic schedule from first of six to last with its shape unchanged. The discovery rate acts through where the search operates, not the trajectory taken, and no single-moment normalisation separates shape from level. These results reinterpret Mareli and Twala (2018), which concluded that an exponentially increasing schedule improves CS. We identify two defects: a criterion that ranks by dispersion rather than quality, and a specification that lets the exponential arm run at a mean pₐ of 0.430 against a nominal cap of 0.25. Under a corrected criterion, that arm ranks last, and a constant schedule at matched level exceeds it. We propose CSAD, a stagnation-adaptive scheme that raises pₐ when the incumbent stalls and decays it when refinement pays; it is competitive at d = 10 but the worst arm at higher dimensions, a failure we diagnose rather than omit. Instrumentation shows the natural explanation—that higher pₐ buys escapes from local optima—is only half correct: it accounts for precision lost on smooth landscapes but not the gain on rugged ones, where diversity and relocations both fall as pₐ rises. Fitness-distance correlation is likewise uncorrelated with its direction, so the effect is reported as a regularity whose mechanism remains open.
