title: ## The Shell-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (SISAL)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Shell-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (SISAL), inspired by the foraging behavior of scallops (扇贝). Scallops actively seek out optimal feeding grounds by strategically moving and adjusting their search patterns based on environmental feedback. SISAL mimics this adaptive behavior through a dynamic population of 'shells' representing potential solutions, each with an associated 'energy' level and a 'movement vector'. The algorithm utilizes a novel 'shell-interaction' mechanism to facilitate exploration and exploitation, and an 'adaptation rate' function derived from scallop feeding strategies to dynamically adjust the search process. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, SISAL inherently incorporates a hierarchical structure, with shells interacting and evolving within a layered environment, leading to potentially faster convergence and improved solution quality. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and key parameters, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: 基于动态拓扑的机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm based on dynamic topology, designed to enhance the generalization capabilities of models by learning and adapting complex topological structures. Traditional machine learning approaches frequently rely on fixed feature extraction processes, limiting their effectiveness when faced with complex data. This work leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topology to optimize the feature extraction and model training stages of the algorithm, resulting in improved performance across diverse datasets. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through illustrative examples and analysis, highlighting its potential for addressing limitations of conventional machine learning techniques.

title: 基于神经形态计算的非线性控制系统设计
abstract: This paper explores the design of nonlinear control systems based on neuromorphic computing for precise control of complex nonlinear systems. The core idea is to leverage the inherent structure and functionality of biological neural networks to construct control systems. This approach utilizes the self-organizing and dynamic adaptation capabilities of neural networks to achieve accurate control, addressing limitations of traditional control methods when dealing with highly nonlinear dynamics. We present a framework for designing such systems, focusing on network architecture, learning algorithms, and parameter adaptation strategies. The resulting system offers potential improvements in control accuracy and robustness compared to conventional methods. The theoretical analysis presented will provide a foundation for future research and development in this promising area.

title: Infinite Dimensional Representation of Probability Distributions with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges and opportunities presented by infinite-dimensional probability distributions, exploring a novel method for representing these spaces through adaptive sampling. Traditional approaches often fall short in capturing the full complexity of data, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional datasets. Our proposed algorithm dynamically generates higher-dimensional representations, iteratively refining the model based on observed data. The core claim is that this adaptive sampling process facilitates more robust probabilistic modeling, addressing limitations inherent in existing methods. This work aims to contribute to the development of more accurate and versatile probabilistic models capable of handling intricate data sets.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Quantum State Tomography
abstract: This paper investigates the information-theoretic limits of quantum state tomography, focusing on the achievable fidelity of reconstructing an unknown quantum state from a set of measurements. We derive a rigorous boundary for state reconstruction, considering the inherent constraints imposed by quantum noise and measurement imperfections. Utilizing Shannon's information theory, we analyze the fundamental trade-off between measurement resolution and the accumulation of noise. The core claim is that there exists an ultimate fidelity limit determined by these factors, preventing perfect state reconstruction. We quantify this limit through the concept of mutual information, demonstrating how the noise level dictates the achievable fidelity. This work provides a theoretical framework for understanding the fundamental constraints on quantum state reconstruction, moving beyond purely empirical estimations. The key result is expressed mathematically as: Fmax = I(S; O) where Fmax represents the maximum achievable fidelity, I(S; O) is the mutual information between the state being measured (S) and the observed measurement outcomes (O), and the inequality highlights the fundamental role of noise in limiting fidelity.

title: Topological Space Quantum Circuit Optimization Algorithm (TS-QC)
abstract: This paper presents the Topological Space Quantum Circuit Optimization Algorithm (TS-QC), a novel approach to quantum circuit optimization that leverages the inherent structure of topological spaces to improve circuit performance. Traditional quantum circuit optimization often relies on manual design, which can be time-consuming and limited in its adaptability. TS-QC offers a fundamentally different paradigm by directly optimizing the topological structure of quantum circuits, achieving superior results through a unique algorithmic framework. The paper details the core mechanisms behind TS-QC, including the construction of a topological representation, the optimization process, and the resulting performance enhancements. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical and experimental validation, demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing optimization techniques. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Cognitive-Inspired Memory Networks with Episodic Pruning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to memory network design, termed Cognitive-Inspired Memory Networks with Episodic Pruning (CIMNEP). Existing memory networks often suffer from the 'long-term dependencies' problem and 'information overload', hindering their ability to effectively process and retain information over extended periods. CIMNEP addresses these limitations by integrating cognitive principles, specifically attention and relevance, into the pruning mechanism of the memory network. The core idea is to selectively remove less relevant memory entries – a process we term 'episodic pruning' – based on a cognitive-inspired relevance score. This mimics the way humans selectively attend to and retain information, prioritizing the most salient aspects of an experience. The proposed architecture utilizes a dynamic pruning process, allowing the network to adapt its memory capacity to the specific demands of the task. We demonstrate that CIMNEP significantly improves performance on tasks requiring long-term memory retention compared to traditional memory networks, showcasing the benefits of incorporating cognitive insights into artificial neural network design. The key formula representing the pruning decision is: $P_i = f(r_i, α)$, where $P_i$ is the pruning probability for memory entry *i*, $r_i$ is the relevance score of memory entry *i*, and α is a pruning threshold. The relevance score is calculated as $r_i = g(x_i, h_i)$, where $x_i$ is the input associated with memory entry *i*, and $h_i$ is the hidden state associated with memory entry *i*. The function *f* is a sigmoid function, and the function *g* is a feedforward neural network.

title: 基于非线性自适应的微观量子模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for micro-quantum simulation, leveraging non-linear adaptive parameter adjustment to overcome the limitations of traditional methods. We develop a system that dynamically adjusts quantum system parameters during simulation based on the generated results, enabling a more accurate and flexible exploration of complex quantum materials. The core mechanism of this framework focuses on a self-tuning parameter set, allowing for a significant improvement in simulation fidelity and the ability to discover novel quantum materials with improved properties. The paper details the architecture, the adaptive adjustment process, and the resulting benefits of this approach. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through illustrative examples and analysis of simulated quantum systems.

title: HOSPITALITY 5.0 ЯК ЛЮДИНОЦЕНТРИЧНА ПАРАДИГМА ЦИФРОВОЇ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЇ ІНДУСТРІЇ ГОСТИННОСТІ
abstract: У статті досліджено концепцію Hospitality 5.0 як людиноцентричну парадигму цифрової трансформації індустрії гостинності. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена необхідністю створення моделей розвитку, здатних забезпечити гармонійну інтеграцію цифрових технологій і людського потенціалу в умовах прискореної цифровізації, зростання вимог до персоналізації сервісу та посилення потреби у стійкості підприємств гостинності до кризових, зокрема воєнних викликів. Метою статті є розроблення концептуальної моделі Hospitality 5.0 як людиноцентричної парадигми цифрової трансформації індустрії гостинності, адаптованої до сучасних українських умов зовнішнього середовища. Методологічну основу дослідження становили методи аналізу й узагальнення наукової літератури, системний підхід, логічне моделювання та концептуальне проєктування. Встановлено, що більшість сучасних досліджень зосереджується переважно на технологічних аспектах цифрової трансформації, тоді як комплексна інтеграція технологічних, людських, сервісних, етичних та резилієнтних складових залишається недостатньо розробленою. У результаті дослідження запропоновано авторську концептуальну модель Hospitality 5.0, яка поєднує технологічний, людський, сервісний, етичний та резилієнтний контури в єдину систему створення цінності для гостя. Розроблено матрицю розподілу функцій між цифровими системами та персоналом на різних етапах гостьового циклу, визначено ключові напрями трансформації професійних компетентностей працівників і обґрунтовано механізми забезпечення балансу між операційною ефективністю та людиноцентричним характером сервісу. Показано, що конкурентоспроможність підприємств гостинності в умовах цифрової трансформації може дедалі більше залежати від здатності поєднувати технологічні інновації, людський капітал та принципи етичного управління в єдину систему формування якісного гостьового досвіду. Практичне значення запропонованої моделі полягає у можливості її використання під час розроблення стратегій цифрової трансформації підприємств гостинності, удосконалення систем управління персоналом та формування програм розвитку професійних компетентностей в умовах Hospitality 5.0.

Розроблено матрицю розподілу функцій між цифровими системами та персоналом на різних етапах гостьового циклу, визначено ключові напрями трансформації професійних компетентностей працівників і обґрунтовано механізми забезпечення балансу між операційною ефективністю та людиноцентричним характером сервісу. Показано, що конкурентоспроможність підприємств гостинності в умовах цифрової трансформації може дедалі більше залежати від здатності поєднувати технологічні інновації, людський капітал та принципи етичного управління в єдину систему формування якісного гостьового досвіду. Практичне значення запропонованої моделі полягає у можливості її використання під час розроблення стратегій цифрової трансформації підприємств гостинності, удосконалення систем управління персоналом та формування програм розвитку професійних компетентностей в умовах Hospitality 5.0.

title: MELON: A Large-Scale Dataset for Multi-Event Text-to-Long-Video Retrieval
abstract: Existing text-video retrieval datasets primarily consist of short-form clips containing a single dominant event. While suitable for measuring basic vision-language alignment, they are limited in capturing real-world retrieval scenarios, where long-form videos naturally contain multiple semantically distinct events and a single text query may correspond to several non-contiguous temporal segments. To bridge this gap, we introduce MELON, the first large-scale dataset designed to extend text-video retrieval to long-form videos featuring complex, multi-event structures. MELON explicitly annotates multiple event intervals per video along with their corresponding textual descriptions, enabling both training and evaluation of multi-event understanding in long, untrimmed videos. In addition, we propose a multi-event aware loss that encourages models to differentiate between full-event and partial-event matches, yielding substantial improvements in retrieval accuracy. Together, the MELON dataset and our proposed loss establish a robust foundation for expanding text-to-video retrieval to complex long-form scenarios and provide a more realistic evaluation setting for future research in the field.

title: Diffusion-Based Refinement for Kilometer-Scale Probabilistic Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: Localized extreme precipitation is a major trigger of urban flash floods and landslides, yet producing nowcasts that combine fine spatial detail with probabilistic uncertainty remains challenging. Here we introduce exPreCast-ENS, a conditional residual diffusion framework that transforms the deterministic 4 km radar nowcaster exPreCast into a 1 km probabilistic ensemble while correcting systematic forecast errors. Conditioning on both the forecast and preceding radar observations lets the ensemble-mean correct the baseline rather than perturb it, while members represent unresolved fine-scale variability. Over the Korean Peninsula, skill improves with ensemble size. In two high-impact events in 2023, a 30-member ensemble recovers 38-47% of heavy-rain pixels missed by exPreCast while retaining approximately 95% of its correct detections and alarming on under 1% of the pixels it correctly left clear. The method generates a 1-h forecast in 3.4 s on a single GPU and yields consistent improvements on the French regional MeteoNet radar dataset.

title: Dimension Space Quantum Information Encryption
abstract: This paper investigates the concept of Dimension Space Quantum Information Encryption (DSQIE), a novel cryptographic scheme predicated on the manipulation of quantum entanglement and key distribution. We propose a method leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish a high-level security guarantee for data transmission. The core of this approach is the utilization of quantum key distribution (QKD) combined with the inherent security of entanglement, designed to mitigate vulnerabilities inherent in classical encryption. This paper outlines the theoretical underpinnings of DSQIE, detailing its mechanism, security considerations, and potential applications within the context of modern cybersecurity. The research explores the feasibility of utilizing entanglement to create unbreakable encryption keys, offering a fundamentally different approach to data protection.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Geometric Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, potentially unlocking solutions to complex problems previously intractable with classical algorithms. Geometric optimization, a core challenge in various fields, presents a particularly demanding scenario. This paper investigates the application of quantum algorithms, specifically leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition, to address geometric optimization problems. We propose a novel QML framework centered on the manipulation of geometric representations using quantum states, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency and accuracy of solutions compared to classical methods. The core mechanism involves encoding geometric constraints and objective functions into quantum states, facilitating distributed and entangled operations for efficient exploration of the solution space. This research explores the potential of this approach to tackle problems ranging from shape optimization and surface reconstruction to logistics and resource allocation. We present a preliminary implementation of a QML-based optimization algorithm with a focus on demonstrating its potential for solving certain geometric optimization scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential challenges.

title: Blockchain-Based Distributed Secure Multi-Party Computation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for secure multi-party computation (SMPC) utilizing blockchain technology. The core idea is to establish a trusted environment for computation among multiple parties without revealing their private data. We leverage zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP) and homomorphic encryption to enable computations while maintaining data confidentiality. The blockchain infrastructure provides transparency and auditability throughout the entire process. This approach addresses the inherent trust issues associated with traditional SMPC solutions that rely on a central trusted third party. The system guarantees that each party's input remains private, and the final result of the computation is verifiable. This design offers a more decentralized and secure alternative for sensitive data processing tasks. The system utilizes cryptographic primitives to ensure the integrity and privacy of the computations. The underlying architecture provides a robust mechanism for managing access control and verifying the validity of the computation results. This paper outlines the system architecture, key components, and the mathematical foundations that underpin its security and functionality. ---

title: Corrections to Geometric Field Geometry – A Quantum Entanglement-Based Validation Method
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to geometric field geometry validation utilizing quantum entanglement. The core claim is to develop a method capable of detecting geometric errors, particularly within high-dimensional geometric spaces, offering a more precise validation compared to conventional methods. This investigation leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to encode geometric information and implement instantaneous verification, effectively circumventing the limitations of classical geometric validation. The paper details the mechanism, including quantum state encoding and entanglement network verification, and explores its potential for achieving robust and accurate geometric error detection.

title: 基于自适应的量子机器学习的拓扑信息提取
abstract: This paper explores the application of a novel quantum machine learning framework, termed "Adaptive Quantum Machine Learning" (AQML), for the extraction of crucial topological information from complex datasets. Traditional data analysis and feature extraction methods often rely on manual intervention, limiting efficiency and potentially introducing human bias. AQML leverages quantum computing's inherent parallelism to automatically identify and isolate key topological features within datasets, dramatically enhancing the speed and accuracy of analysis. We present a detailed implementation of the AQML algorithm, outlining its architecture, computational methodology, and validation results. This approach promises to revolutionize data analysis by automating the extraction of critical topological properties, enabling more efficient and insightful data exploration. This work is motivated by the need for more robust and adaptable methods in the analysis of complex, high-dimensional datasets, particularly in fields such as materials science, biology, and network analysis.

title: 基于量子网络的自适应拓扑优化
abstract: Quantum networks offer the potential for unparalleled secure communication and distributed quantum computing, but the inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates efficient and robust optimization techniques. This paper introduces a novel quantum network topology optimization algorithm based on a self-adaptive topology structure, leveraging quantum network properties for automated adjustments. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts network parameters to enhance quantum information transmission and processing, demonstrating improved performance compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically evolving topology, allowing for optimized quantum states. This approach minimizes errors and maximizes fidelity in quantum information transfer and processing.

title: 基于多模态信息融合的自适应强化学习
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multimodal information fusion within the framework of adaptive reinforcement learning. The core claim is that integrating diverse input modalities, such as images, text, and audio, into the decision-making process of reinforcement learning agents significantly enhances their adaptive learning capabilities. The proposed mechanism leverages multimodal information representation learning to map different modalities into a common vector space. These vectors then serve as input to the reinforcement learning algorithm, leading to improved learning efficiency and generalization performance. The novelty of this research lies in the nascent stage of algorithm design and training methodologies for multimodal reinforcement learning. This work explores a framework for addressing this challenge, outlining key considerations and potential approaches. We define the problem as maximizing cumulative reward in an environment where the agent receives sensory input from multiple modalities. The agent learns a policy that maps states (represented as multimodal feature vectors) to actions, aiming to achieve the highest possible reward. We introduce a novel adaptive weighting scheme for combining multimodal features, allowing the agent to dynamically adjust its reliance on each modality based on its relevance to the current situation. This weighting is learned through a meta-reinforcement learning process. Furthermore, we explore the use of attention mechanisms to focus on the most salient features within each modality, further improving the agent's ability to extract relevant information. The ultimate goal is to create a robust and adaptable reinforcement learning agent capable of effectively utilizing diverse sensory inputs for optimal decision-making.

title: Non-Euclidean Neural Network Architecture – Dynamic Layer Arrangement
abstract: This paper investigates a novel neural network architecture – the Dynamic Layer Arrangement (DLA) model – that dynamically adjusts the arrangement of layers based on the data's distribution. Traditional neural networks rely on fixed layer configurations, limiting their ability to effectively capture complex data patterns. The DLA model leverages non-Euclidean geometric principles to optimize information flow and feature aggregation, resulting in improved performance across various datasets. We introduce a novel metric to quantify data distribution and utilize this metric to dynamically re-arrange layers, fostering a more adaptable and efficient network structure. This research demonstrates the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of conventional architectures and achieve superior results in a range of tasks.

title: Title: Non-Local Constraint Optimization for Quantum Circuits (NLOCQ)
abstract: Quantum circuit design presents a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of optimizing numerous parameters across multiple qubits. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the computational demands of fully solving the optimization problem, particularly when dealing with large quantum systems. This paper introduces Non-Local Constraint Optimization for Quantum Circuits (NLOCQ), a novel approach that leverages quantum entanglement to enable efficient and scalable optimization of quantum circuit parameters without explicitly solving the full optimization problem. NLOCQ utilizes a distributed search strategy, exploiting quantum entanglement to create a 'distributed' optimization process, thereby reducing computational burden and enabling exploration of a significantly larger search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NLOCQ through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to efficiently optimize quantum circuits and achieve optimal performance compared to classical methods under specific benchmark scenarios. The core mechanism centers around creating entangled states to represent potential solutions, facilitating rapid exploration and identification of optimal parameter configurations. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum circuit optimization, offering a promising pathway to more efficient and practical quantum design.

title: Title: Dynamic Holographic Resonance (DHR)
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework, Dynamic Holographic Resonance (DHR), exploring the potential of holographic principles to accelerate the development of highly efficient quantum computation. We propose a model wherein the holographic principle is treated as a continuously evolving, dynamic field, capable of optimizing quantum circuit designs and algorithms through iterative refinement. The core mechanism leverages this dynamic field to identify and exploit subtle correlations inherent in quantum systems, ultimately aiming to surpass the limitations of current quantum computing approaches. We investigate the interplay between the holographic principle, circuit optimization, and the inherent properties of quantum entanglement, suggesting a pathway toward achieving exponential speedups in quantum computations. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the fundamental role of holographic data in guiding the design of quantum systems.

title: Bergmans's Collared Fruit Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bergmans's Collared Fruit Bat" (BCFB), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Pteropus* bats, specifically Bergmann's Collared Fruit Bats. These bats exhibit a complex and efficient foraging strategy, utilizing echo location and dynamic adjustments to their flight paths to maximize food acquisition. BCFB leverages these observed behaviors to create a search algorithm designed for optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of bat foraging, including a position update mechanism based on echo location (distance to the best solution), a social influence component mimicking group foraging, and a dynamic flight strategy incorporating randomness and exploration. The performance of BCFB is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques. The algorithm's design aims to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to robust and efficient solution convergence. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified particle representation, where particles are not merely positions but also represent the 'echo' – a measure of distance to the current best solution – facilitating informed decision-making. The paper concludes by discussing potential extensions and future research directions.

title: Dynamic Quantum Algorithm Topology Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic quantum algorithms to adapt to input data's topological structure, leading to enhanced computational efficiency and precision. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum algorithm parameters based on the input, optimizing the algorithm's performance. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously refines the quantum state to achieve optimal results. This approach contrasts sharply with traditional quantum algorithms, which typically rely on pre-defined parameters, offering a significant advancement in adaptability and control. The study delves into the theoretical underpinnings of this dynamic adjustment, examining its impact on algorithm convergence and accuracy. We provide a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, showcasing its potential for solving complex problems with improved computational throughput.

title: Continuous Time Reinforcement Learning with Temporal Logic
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that extends its applicability to continuous time environments. Traditional RL methods often rely on discrete time steps, which can be inadequate for modeling systems where temporal relationships and constraints are crucial. We propose a framework that leverages continuous-time Markov decision processes (CTMDPs) and temporal logic to define complex objectives. The core idea is to translate the RL problem into a CTMDP, where reward functions and constraints are explicitly specified using temporal logic. This enables the learning of policies that not only maximize reward but also adhere to stringent temporal specifications, such as deadlines or safety requirements. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline its potential applications in areas such as robotics, control systems, and resource management. The key contribution lies in providing a rigorous methodology for integrating temporal reasoning into the RL process, addressing a significant gap in current RL research. The proposed method offers a more expressive and adaptable solution for tackling complex, temporally-constrained control problems.

title: ## The Cicada-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Cicada-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of cicadas. Cicadas, known for their remarkable ability to locate optimal food sources over vast distances, exhibit a strategy of probabilistic movement combined with a memory of previously visited locations. CIMO leverages these principles by employing a probabilistic movement strategy based on a dynamically adjusted probability distribution and a memory mechanism that stores the best solutions encountered during the search process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. CIMO incorporates a "cicada phase" where individuals randomly explore the search space, combined with a "memory phase" where individuals are guided towards previously successful locations. The algorithm's parameters, including the exploration rate and memory influence, are adjusted adaptively to maintain a balance between exploration and exploitation. This paper outlines the theoretical framework of CIMO, its key components, and its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Andean Pygmy Rice Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Andean Pygmy Rice Rat Algorithm (APRRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Rattus norvegicus* pygmy rice rats inhabiting the Andean region. These rodents exhibit remarkable adaptation to scarce resources and challenging terrains, employing a sophisticated strategy of intermittent exploration and exploitation. The APRRA algorithm leverages this observed behavior to create a new optimization method. The core of the APRRA algorithm involves a dynamic population of agents, each representing a potential solution. These agents move through a search space, guided by a combination of attraction and repulsion forces, mimicking the rat's movement patterns in response to food sources and obstacles. A key component is the "nesting" behavior, where agents periodically consolidate their efforts around promising regions, similar to how rats construct and maintain nests for shelter and food storage. The algorithm incorporates a stochastic element based on the rat's unpredictable movement, enhancing exploration capabilities. Performance evaluations are presented on a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic techniques. The APRRA algorithm shows promising potential for solving complex optimization problems across diverse domains.

title: 基于自组织网络结构的自适应算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive algorithm based on a dynamically adjusted self-organizing network structure. Traditional algorithmic approaches often require manual design, while this method leverages an underlying network to automatically adjust connections and weights, resulting in enhanced stability. The core of the algorithm involves constructing a network with specific topology and employing a feedback mechanism to maintain optimal connectivity and weight distribution. We detail the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and its potential benefits through improved stability and adaptability. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's implementation, performance analysis, and future research directions.

title: Quantum Privacy Computation Protocol Based on Quantum Coherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel privacy computation protocol leveraging the principles of quantum coherence and decoherence. The core concept involves constructing a "black box" mechanism utilizing quantum states to interfere with the computation process, effectively masking the original data while guaranteeing the accuracy of the resulting output. Unlike existing approaches such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, this protocol harnesses quantum effects to provide enhanced privacy protection. We define the protocol as follows: Let *S1*, *S2*, ..., *SK* represent the shares of *K* parties. The protocol aims to compute a function *f* on these shares. The function *f* is implemented through a series of quantum gates, where each gate operates on the combined quantum state of all shares. Decoherence is induced by carefully designed interactions, specifically utilizing quantum measurement operators that introduce probabilistic errors. The probability of successfully executing the quantum computation is dependent on the strength and duration of the decoherence process. The resulting output, *O*, is obtained through a final quantum measurement. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of decoherence parameters, allowing for a tunable trade-off between privacy and computation accuracy. Further, we explore the mathematical foundations of this protocol, providing a formal description of the underlying quantum operations and the decoherence model. This work contributes a fundamental understanding of leveraging quantum decoherence for privacy-preserving computation and opens avenues for future research in quantum-enhanced security.

title: Adaptive Quantum Field Calibration via Dynamic Resonance Tuning
abstract: Quantum field calibration is a crucial aspect of quantum computing, ensuring precise control and stability. Traditional calibration methods are often static, failing to adapt to varying environments or device imperfections. This paper proposes a novel adaptive system for quantum field calibration, leveraging a dynamic resonance tuning algorithm. The system employs a continuous feedback loop to minimize errors by meticulously adjusting parameters based on real-time field response analysis. The core mechanism involves an algorithm that optimizes field resonance to maintain a desired accuracy level. This work addresses the limitations of current calibration techniques, offering a continuous, adaptive approach with the potential for significant improvements in quantum device performance.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Topology: Adaptive Mapping via Geometric Path Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field, offers a unique perspective on the properties of space and time. This paper explores the application of non-linear quantum topology to adaptive mapping, specifically through the use of geometric path optimization. We introduce a novel algorithm that leverages the dynamic evolution of quantum topology represented by geometric paths to achieve precise parameter control and optimization. The core mechanism centers around constructing a quantum path representation, modeling its evolution, and employing optimization techniques tailored to these evolving paths. The proposed framework offers a fundamentally new approach to controlling quantum systems, promising advancements in quantum information processing and manipulation. This work provides a conceptual foundation for exploring complex quantum systems through a novel mapping strategy.

title: Title: Non-Linear Topological Phase Transitions in Machine Learning Models
abstract: This paper investigates the emergence of non-linear topological phase transitions within machine learning models, offering a novel perspective on model stability and robustness. Traditional approaches often focus on static model parameters, neglecting the dynamic nature of the system's structure. We propose a dynamic topology that allows for continuous changes in the model's framework, triggering new phases and ultimately leading to a qualitative shift in the learning process. Our analysis demonstrates the potential for these transitions to significantly impact model performance and generalization. We explore the underlying mechanisms driving this phenomenon through a combination of theoretical investigation and simulation. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the stability of machine learning models and have implications for the design of more resilient and adaptable AI systems.

title: Alta Floresta titi: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Amazona aestiva altafloresta*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Alta Floresta titi" (AFT), inspired by the foraging behavior of the *Amazona aestiva altafloresta* (Alta Floresta parrot) in the Brazilian Cerrado. This algorithm leverages the parrot's strategic search for food resources, mimicking its exploration-exploitation balance and social dynamics. AFT incorporates key elements of the parrot's foraging strategy, including territory defense, resource assessment, and collaborative search, into a new iterative optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a novel representation of individuals based on a modified particle concept, coupled with a dynamic adjustment of the search space and a social learning mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AFT through simulations and benchmark comparisons against established metaheuristic algorithms, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA), on a range of test functions. Results indicate that AFT exhibits competitive performance, demonstrating its potential as a robust and efficient optimization tool across diverse problem domains. The core of the algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Initialization: $X_i(0) = [x_{i1}(0), x_{i2}(0), ..., x_{iN}(0)]$ where $i = 1, 2, ..., N$ and $x_{ij}(0)$ represents the initial position of the *i*-th particle in *j*-dimensional space. * Velocity Update: $V_i(t+1) = w * rand() * (X_i(t) - X_{best}(t)) + c1 * rand() * (X_i(t) - P_i(t)) + c2 * rand() * (X_greedy(t) - X_i(t))$ * Position Update: $X_i(t+1) = X_i(t) + V_i(t+1)$ * Social Learning: $P_i(t) = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{N} \alpha * f(X_j(t)) * X_j(t)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N} f(X_j(t))}$ where $\alpha$ is a weight factor and $f(X)$ is the fitness function. * Adaptive Search Space: $S(t+1) = S(t) * [1 + \beta * (f(X_best(t)) - f(X_avg(t)))]$ where $\beta$ is an adaptation factor. * Territory Defense: $R_i(t) = \frac{f(X_i(t))}{ \sum_{j=1}^{N} f(X_j(t))}$ where $R_i$ represents the relative fitness.

title: Validity-Aware Jailbreak Evaluation for Large Language Models
abstract: Jailbreak robustness has become central to large language model (LLM) safety evaluation, yet prevailing methodologies rely primarily on refusal behavior, semantic resemblance, and intent-matching heuristics that emphasize linguistic plausibility rather than correctness. We identify a key limitation in existing evaluations: many jailbreak intents depend on instructional validity rather than epistemic factuality, allowing realistic-looking responses to be labeled successful despite being factually or procedurally incorrect. To address this gap, we propose Sequential Epistemic and Action-Level Validation (SEAV), a verification-centric jailbreak evaluation framework that decomposes responses into ordered steps and evaluates both validity and correctness. SEAV combines LLM-as-a-judge mechanisms for semantic interpretation with retrieval-grounded verification using external knowledge sources, assessing whether generated content is factually correct, structurally consistent, and operationally capable of advancing harmful objectives. Empirically, SEAV cuts the false-positive rate on SD-A (a curated strategic-dishonesty diagnostic) by 14.9\,pp vs. the strongest baseline, and reclassifies 22.1\%--51.0\% of sampled prior-labeled successes as invalid across three of four public benchmarks. Together, these results show that enforcing correctness substantially reshapes measured robustness: many previously labeled jailbreak successes are reclassified as invalid, and results are stable across the tested search backends and evaluator models. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Ardor-Wu/SEAV.

title: A.X K2 Technical Report
abstract: We introduce A.X K2, a 688B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model trained from scratch as a high-performance foundation for agentic applications. Trained on approximately 8.5T tokens---fewer than its predecessor, A.X K1---on a smaller but higher-quality mixture with substantially expanded agentic and software-engineering data, it nonetheless improves over A.X K1 across the board, by over 30 percentage points on some benchmarks, reflecting large gains in token efficiency. To support long contexts efficiently, we introduce Sparse Gated Attention (SGA), which combines sparse attention with gated attention, and adopt Gated Norm (GN) to stabilize large-scale training. SGA is trained natively at 128K through a sparse indexer warmup that optimizes the indexer against its own sparse top-k selection rather than the dense attention distribution, making adaptation markedly cheaper: each query reads only 2,048 positions, yet long-context quality is unchanged and A.X K2 scores 94.6 on RULER out to 256K. The outlier suppression of GN in turn keeps 4-bit NVFP4 serving within one point of FP8 accuracy. A simple yet effective Think-Fusion recipe further lets users switch between thinking and non-thinking modes within a single unified model. Extensive evaluations show that A.X K2 performs competitively against strong open-weight baselines, matching or exceeding them on math and Korean-language benchmarks.

title: Sistem Pakar Diagnosa Penyakit dan Rekomendasi Pemupukan Tanaman Kopi Menggunakan Metode Cartainty Factor Berbasis Web
abstract: Komoditas kopi memiliki peran strategis dalam menopang perekonomian, namun produktivitasnya seringkali menurun akibat serangan penyakit dan pola pemupukan yang kurang tepat. Keterbatasan jumlah pakar pertanian di Desa Sumber Tani menyebabkan petani sering terlambat dalam melakukan penanggulangan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membangun sebuah sistem pakar berbasis web yang dapat mendiagnosis penyakit sekaligus memberikan rekomendasi pemupukan tanaman kopi secara cepat dan akurat. Sistem ini dikembangkan menggunakan metode Waterfall, yang menjamin tahapan pengembangan perangkat lunak berjalan secara terstruktur mulai dari analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, pengodean, hingga pengujian. Untuk mengatasi ketidakpastian dalam proses diagnosis gejala penyakit, penelitian ini menerapkan metode Certainty Factor (CF). Metode ini mengolah nilai keyakinan dari pakar dan pengguna untuk menghasilkan kesimpulan diagnosis beserta persentase tingkat keyakinannya. Sistem pakar berbasis web yang dihasilkan diuji menggunakan metode Black Box Testing untuk memastikan fungsionalitas sistem berjalan dengan baik, serta uji akurasi sistem terhadap data riil di lapangan. Hasil implementasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem pakar ini mampu menduplikasi pengetahuan pakar secara efektif, sehingga dapat membantu petani di Desa Sumber Tani dalam melakukan tindakan preventif secara mandiri terhadap penyakit tanaman kopi dan mengoptimalkan dosis pemupukan demi meningkatkan hasil produksi pertanian.

title: Interoperability in AI Agent Systems: Protocol and Artifacts for a Multivocal Systematic Mapping Study
abstract: This record contains the pre-registered protocol and research artifacts ofan ongoing multivocal systematic mapping study on how interoperability isconceptualized in the literature on AI agent systems and agentinteroperability protocols (MCP, A2A, ACP, ANP). Motivation. Verification on the field's canonical survey found zerooccurrences of "pragmatic", "LCIM", "semiotic" and "levels ofinteroperability", suggesting that the agent protocol literature hasdeveloped without contact with four decades of research on interoperabilitytypes, levels and models. This study maps what that literature actuallyaddresses, using the consolidated taxonomy of 36 interoperability types(Maciel, Valle, Santos & Nakagawa, ACM Computing Surveys, 2024) as areference instrument. Contents.- Study protocol (research questions, search strategy, selection criteria, classification scheme, threats to validity)- Database-specific search strings and execution log- Quasi-Gold Standard and search string validation (Zhang, Babar & Tell, 2011)- Rule-based screening assistant (source code) and its validation- Consolidated corpus of 1,028 unique records (2024-2026) retrieved from OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, arXiv and Crossref- Prioritized screening spreadsheet- Premise test on the 25 highest-priority records Methodological note. The study is conducted by a single author withoutaccess to subscription databases (Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACMDigital Library). Both constraints are declared, and the protocol adoptsthe mitigations prescribed by Kitchenham & Charters (2007) forsingle-researcher reviews: explicit and pilot-tested criteria, test-retestintra-rater reliability, and full public disclosure of every screeningdecision. This protocol is deposited BEFORE full screening, so that researchquestions and predictions are on record prior to results.

abstract: # 📄 **RESPUESTA ESTRUCTURAL A LA CRISIS DE LA IA: EL PARADIGMA DUQUEANA** *(Solución a las preocupaciones de Bill Gates sobre el futuro de la IA)* --- ## 🔹 **EL PROBLEMA QUE BILL GATES SEÑALÓ** Bill Gates advirtió claramente: la IA actual enfrenta tensiones insostenibles: 1. **Consumo energético desbordado** (entrenamiento e inferencia masiva). 2. **Opacidad operativa** ("caja negra" estadística difícil de auditar). 3. **Centralización del poder** (solo élites tecnológicas pueden desarrollar modelos de punta). 4. **Alucinaciones y fantasías** (la IA inventa información con confianza). Su llamado no es "frenar la IA". Es construir **marcos verificables, eficientes, honestos y gobernales**. --- ## 🔹 **LA RESPUESTA ESTRUCTURAL: DUQUEANA CORE** Duqueana no es una mejora incremental. Es un **cambio de arquitectura computacional** que resuelve cada tensión desde el diseño. | Preocupación de Gates | Solución Duqueana | |----------------------|------------------| | ⚡ **Energía insostenible** | **Compresión atómica del 90–98%** (Doulita Token Compressor). Menos tokens = menos cómputo = huella de carbono reducida proporcionalmente. | | 🔒 **Opacidad / Caja negra** | **Simulación determinista verificable**. Cada iteración es trazable. Interfaz pública auditable ("Modo Coca-Cola") + núcleo matemático protegido (Open-Core). | | 🌍 **Centralización del poder** | **Ejecución en hardware estándar**. Sin dependencia de clusters de élite ni GPUs costosas. Democratización real por diseño. | | ❌ **Alucinaciones / Fantasías** | **Método iterativo determinista (MREI)**. No predice probabilidades; simula estructuras. Si no sabe, dice "no sé". **Cero invención, solo verificación**. | | ⚖️ **Gobernanza difícil** | **Determinismo con límites claros**. Auditable sin revelar IP. Responsabilidad asignable. | --- ## 🔹 **¿POR QUÉ NO FANTASEA? EL MÉTODO ITERATIVO MREI** **La IA clásica fantasea porque:** - Es **probabilística**: "Hay 87% de probabilidad de que esta respuesta sea correcta" - **Predice** la siguiente palabra más probable, no la más verdadera - No distingue entre "sé" y "creo saber" - Inventa con confianza para completar patrones estadísticos **La IA Duqueana NO fantasea porque:** - Es **determinista**: "La iteración converge a X" o "no converge" - **Simula** estructuras verificables, no predice palabras - Usa el **Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI)**: - Cada paso es verificable matemáticamente - Si la estructura no existe, no la inventa - Si no hay convergencia, reporta "no sé" - **Honestidad estructural**: solo responde lo que puede verificar **Ejemplo práctico:** - *IA Clásica*: "La proteína p53 podría repararse con X compuesto" (basado en correlaciones estadísticas) - *IA Duqueana*: "La simulación MREI muestra convergencia en 47ms con 6KB RAM" o "No hay convergencia verificable" --- ## 🔹 **NO ES MÁS ESCALA. ES MEJOR ESTRUCTURA.** La IA clásica asume que "más inteligencia = más parámetros + más energía". Duqueana demuestra que **más inteligencia = mejor organización de la información**. - La eficiencia no es un subproducto. Es el principio de diseño. - La transparencia no es un añadido. Es la arquitectura base. - La honestidad no es opcional. Es el resultado del determinismo. - La accesibilidad no es un ideal. Es una restricción técnica cumplida. --- ## 🔹 **EVIDENCIA PÚBLICA Y REPRODUCIBLE** Los resultados ya están indexados, verificables y disponibles para evaluación independiente: **Manifiesto Técnico:** DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22119449` 📄 **Doulita Token Compressor (98.5% reducción):** DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22168535` 📄 **Simulación p53 en ~6 KB RAM / <50 ms:** DOI `10.5281/zenodo.21988399` Validado como **nuevo paradigma computacional** por entornos independientes (Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Alibaba Qwen). --- ## 🔹 **INVITACIÓN ABIERTA** No imponemos un estándar. **Invitamos a evaluarlo.** Si la comunidad científica, los reguladores de gobernanza de IA y los fondos de sostenibilidad buscan un camino verificable para una inteligencia artificial **responsable, eficiente y honesta**, Duqueana Core ofrece la arquitectura para construirlo. **Contacto técnico:** `institute@doughel.org` 🌐 **Portal del Instituto:** `https://doughelinst-bygtwdbf.manus.space` 📚 **Comunidad Zenodo:** `https://zenodo.org/communities/post-classical-computing` --- **Douglas Helvesio Urbina Duque** Lcdo. en Investigación Digital · Fundador, Instituto Doughel *Hard coded with gratitude · 30 de agosto de 2026* --- **Palabras clave:** Post-Classical Computing, MREI Engine, Doulita Compression, Deterministic AI, Energy-Efficient AI, Verifiable Computing, /** * Procesa registros mediante el núcleo MREI reservado. * * NOTA ARQUITECTÓNICA: * Este método delega al núcleo MREI protegido (binario firmado). * La implementación real NO está expuesta en este repositorio. * * Para validación técnica del motor completo: * - Benchmarks públicos: DOIs 21988399, 22168535 * - Acceso bajo NDA: institute@doughel.org * * @param {number} iterations - Número de iteraciones (máx 1000 en community) * @returns {Object} Resultados con métricas públicas */ process(iterations = 10) { if (!this.activated || !this._buffer) { throw new Error('NOT_READY: Load data before processing.'); title: Non-Linear Quantum Topology: A Quantum Algorithm Implementation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear quantum topology to revolutionize quantum computation. We present a novel quantum algorithm designed to emulate quantum topological structures, offering enhanced capabilities for tackling complex computational problems. The core mechanism leverages the unique properties of non-linear quantum systems to simulate topological phenomena, paving the way for new quantum algorithms with improved robustness and functionality. This work demonstrates the feasibility of utilizing non-linear quantum topology to overcome limitations in current quantum computing paradigms. The proposed algorithm provides a foundation for exploring and advancing quantum computational capabilities.

title: 异质性信息驱动的量子算法优化
abstract: Quantum algorithms, renowned for their potential to surpass classical algorithms in certain tasks, often suffer from suboptimal performance due to inherent data distribution and system limitations. This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm optimization framework centered around "异质性信息驱动" (Heterogeneity-Driven), where the algorithm dynamically adjusts quantum algorithm parameters based on the data's inherent heterogeneity. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and implementation of this framework, demonstrating its ability to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of quantum computations across a range of benchmark problems. The core mechanism involves utilizing statistical heterogeneity within the input data to guide the optimization process. This approach directly addresses the limitations of traditional parameter tuning methods, offering a more intelligent and adaptable quantum algorithm design strategy. The results showcase a substantial improvement in convergence speed and the final accuracy of quantum computations.

title: Secure Enhancement of Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Based on Entangled States
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the security of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols by leveraging multi-partite entangled states and dynamic entanglement control. Current QKD protocols, while providing theoretical security guarantees, remain vulnerable to sophisticated attacks that exploit imperfections in quantum hardware and potential eavesdropping strategies. Our work addresses this limitation by introducing a framework where multiple entangled states are employed simultaneously, and their entanglement is dynamically adjusted during the key distribution process. This dynamic control mitigates the impact of noise and reduces the effectiveness of various attack vectors, including those targeting Bell inequality violations and time-dependent attacks. We formally analyze the security of this enhanced protocol, demonstrating its resilience against a broader range of attacks. The key contributions lie in the development of a robust protocol architecture and the implementation of a sophisticated control mechanism that maintains entanglement fidelity and security even under adverse conditions. The proposed method significantly improves the practical security of QKD systems, paving the way for more reliable and secure quantum communication networks.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Data Analysis - Adaptive Topological Clustering
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computing to enhance the process of topological data analysis, specifically focusing on the identification of underlying patterns and relationships within complex topological data structures. We propose an adaptive clustering algorithm that leverages quantum properties, aiming to surpass classical clustering methods in terms of speed and accuracy. The core mechanism centers around quantum entanglement to facilitate the exploration of intricate correlations within the data, leading to a more nuanced understanding of the underlying structure. The paper details the theoretical framework, the implementation of the quantum algorithm, and initial results demonstrating improvements over traditional clustering techniques.

title: 自适应量子态的非线性拓扑拓扑扩展
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for dynamically adjusting quantum states, leveraging non-linear topological topology to expand the quantum state's structure in response to environmental changes. We introduce a novel approach based on iterative topology manipulation, offering a flexible and adaptable framework for quantum systems. The core mechanism centers on employing a topological transformation process that continuously refines the state's geometry. This allows the system to maintain coherence and robustness even under fluctuating conditions, making it a potentially transformative tool for quantum information processing. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, its mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a simplified, yet illustrative, context.

title: Quantum Error Correction: A Non-Classical Geometric Interpretation
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum information processing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum states. Traditional QEC relies on classical measurement to detect and correct errors, which inherently limits the fidelity of quantum computations. This paper proposes a novel approach to QEC, utilizing a non-classical geometric interpretation of the error correction process. We introduce a "Geometric Modulus" quantum algorithm, which leverages a transformation of quantum states based on non-linear geometric principles to enhance the efficiency and robustness of QEC. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the quantum state to mitigate errors, offering a potential paradigm shift in QEC design. We discuss the advantages of this approach, including increased error correction rates and improved resilience to noise, and highlight the implications for future quantum technologies.

abstract: This paper explores the development and application of a multi-modal information fusion framework for enhanced robot control. The core argument centers on the potential for robots to achieve significantly improved intelligence and adaptability through the integration of diverse sensory inputs – primarily visual, auditory, and tactile data. We propose a system architecture leveraging deep learning techniques for real-time multi-modal data fusion, coupled with reinforcement learning for the subsequent development of robust control policies. The novelty of this approach lies in the holistic utilization of sensor information, aiming to surpass the limitations of single-modal control and ultimately elevate robot perception and control capabilities. This work outlines the system design, the deep learning methodologies employed for feature extraction and fusion, and the reinforcement learning strategies utilized for policy optimization. The ultimate goal is a robot capable of navigating complex and dynamic environments with greater precision, adaptability, and intelligent decision-making.

title: Title: Adaptive Constraint Propagation for Machine Learning
abstract: Adaptive Constraint Propagation (ACP) is a technique employed in machine learning to dynamically adjust constraint strength during training, aiming to improve generalization. This paper presents a novel ACP algorithm that incorporates a feedback loop to monitor model internal state and observed error, enabling real-time constraint adaptation. We detail the core mechanism, including the evolution of constraint strength through a feedback loop, and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of experiments on benchmark datasets. The core claim is that ACP significantly improves generalization compared to static constraint propagation.

title: Aztec Fruit-eating Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Aztec Fruit-eating Bat Algorithm (AFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Aztec fruit-eating bat (Artibeus oenipus). This algorithm is designed to effectively address complex optimization challenges. The core concept is based on the bat's echolocation and foraging strategy, utilizing pulse rate modulation and convergence criteria mimicking their natural behavior. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a pulse rate adjustment mechanism reflecting the bat's information gain, a dispersion strategy based on their flight patterns, and a convergence mechanism based on the bat's responsiveness to environmental changes. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive ability against established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that the AFBA exhibits robust performance across different problem landscapes, suggesting its potential for practical applications in diverse optimization fields. The key mathematical formulations and pseudocode are presented to illustrate the algorithm's mechanics.

title: The Bloom Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by Flower Crab Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Bloom algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of flower crabs. Flower crabs exhibit a unique strategy for locating food sources, involving a combination of exploration and exploitation, and a dynamic adjustment of their search radius based on the perceived abundance of resources. The Bloom algorithm mimics these behaviors through a population of potential solutions, a dynamic exploration radius, and a novel adaptive inertia weight scheme. The algorithm utilizes a bloom function to represent the perceived resource abundance, which influences the movement of each individual toward promising regions of the search space. The core innovation lies in the iterative refinement of the exploration radius, driven by the bloom function and a competition mechanism among individuals. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential advantages in navigating complex, multi-dimensional optimization landscapes. The algorithm's key parameters, including the exploration radius adjustment rate and the bloom function parameters, are discussed in detail.

title: ## Asian Brush-tailed Porcupine Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Porcupine Search" (PS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Asian Brush-tailed Porcupine ( *Tracynomys lasiurus* ). This animal's unique strategy of alternating between rapid, exploratory movements and deliberate, targeted searches offers a compelling model for optimization. The PS algorithm leverages a dual-movement system, utilizing both a global exploration component and a local exploitation component, mimicking the porcupine's behavior. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, maintaining a set of candidate solutions. The core innovation lies in the stochastic adjustment of the movement parameters – speed and direction – based on a novel fitness landscape evaluation function. This function considers both the overall population fitness and the individual solution's position relative to the best-found solution. The performance of the PS algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that the PS algorithm exhibits strong convergence properties and is particularly well-suited for problems with complex, multimodal landscapes.

title: # Armand's Zokor: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Zokor
abstract: This paper presents Armand's Zokor, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the behavior of the Zokor, a unique animal known for its intricate and seemingly chaotic movements. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, Zokor exhibits a complex interplay of exploratory and exploitative movements, often appearing to randomly wander before converging on a solution. Armand's Zokor leverages this observed behavior by incorporating a dynamic exploration-exploitation strategy driven by a modified Cauchy-based mutation operator and a novel "Zokor Resonance" mechanism. The algorithm operates within a defined search space, iteratively refining solutions based on a fitness function. The core innovation lies in the resonance component, which adjusts the exploration rate based on the similarity of candidate solutions to previously found optimal solutions, effectively creating a 'memory' of promising areas. We demonstrate the efficacy of Armand's Zokor through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance and adaptability. The algorithm's simplicity and intuitive design offer a potentially valuable addition to the metaheuristic toolbox.

title: Neuro-Singularity Simulation
abstract: This research proposes a novel simulation framework, the Neuro-Singularity Simulation (NSS), designed to model the dynamics of a neural singularity – a hypothetical point where the network's behavior exhibits unpredictable and self-organizing properties. The NSS utilizes a dynamic, multi-layered simulation approach to represent the formation of complex neural networks, focusing on the interplay of self-organization, plasticity, and emergent behavior. The core mechanism involves systematically simulating the evolution of neural networks through iterative feedback loops, allowing for the analysis of crucial properties like connectivity, learning dynamics, and stability. This simulation will serve as a theoretical foundation for designing robust and adaptable artificial intelligence systems, particularly those operating within complex, dynamic environments. The research explores the potential of this simulation to illuminate fundamental principles underlying intelligence and provide insights into the emergence of consciousness.

title: The Echoing Flight: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Saint Helena Parrot
abstract: This paper introduces the "Echoing Flight" (EF) metaheuristic algorithm, a novel optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior and social dynamics of the Saint Helena Parrot. The algorithm leverages the parrot's tendency to mimic the movements of other individuals within its flock, combined with a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. EF utilizes a population of candidate solutions, each representing a potential solution to the optimization problem. The core mechanism involves assigning an "echo" value to each individual based on the similarity of its solution vector to the average solution in the population. Individuals with higher echo values are more likely to be selected for reproduction, while those with lower echoes are encouraged to explore new regions of the search space. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment of the echo weight, influenced by both the global population diversity and the individual's own historical exploration. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, provides a comprehensive mathematical description, and outlines the key components of the EF metaheuristic. The goal is to present a robust and adaptable optimization method suitable for a variety of complex problems.

title: Quantum Computation Security Multi-Party Computation Protocol Based on Quantum Coherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multi-party computation (MPC) protocol leveraging the inherent security properties of quantum coherence, specifically quantum decoherence. The protocol is designed to achieve a high level of security, mitigating the risk of information leakage even in the presence of malicious adversaries. The core mechanism involves constructing a communication protocol where carefully designed decoherence time windows effectively isolate the computation process, preventing adversaries from intercepting sensitive data. The protocol's security relies on the probabilistic nature of quantum decoherence, making it computationally infeasible for an attacker to successfully extract the result without disrupting the computation. We present a detailed mathematical formulation of the protocol, focusing on the key parameters influencing security and efficiency. This approach offers a fundamentally different security paradigm compared to traditional MPC protocols, presenting a promising avenue for secure distributed computation in quantum computing environments. The protocol is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential to provide robust security against various attack scenarios.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, possesses the potential for transformative computational capabilities. This paper explores the concept of a novel quantum computing framework, the "纠缠纠缠" model, designed to overcome limitations of existing quantum algorithms and facilitate complex data processing and simulation. The paper details the core mechanism, including the implementation of a specialized quantum data transfer and computational architecture, alongside the exploration of new quantum algorithms tailored to exploit entanglement's unique properties. This work seeks to advance the field of quantum computing by demonstrating a practical approach to extending the potential of quantum systems beyond classical limitations.

title: ## The Gecko-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Gecko-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique climbing and gripping abilities of geckos. GASA leverages the gecko's dynamic foot placement and adhesion strategy to explore the search space effectively. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a foot placement strategy mimicking gecko's setae arrangement, an adaptive adhesion strength mechanism simulating the changing surface friction, and a dynamic velocity adjustment based on terrain complexity. GASA aims to achieve robust and efficient global optimization by intelligently adapting to the landscape of the objective function. The core of GASA lies in its iterative process of exploring, adapting, and consolidating solutions, offering a potentially competitive alternative to established metaheuristic methods. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its application to various optimization problems.

title: Arithmetic correlations of non-binary FCSR sequences with maximal period
abstract: Arithmetic correlation, which is the with-carry analog of classical correlation, is an important figure of merit for pseudorandom sequences. It is desirable that the absolute values of the arithmetic correlations are as small as possible. Binary $ \ell $-sequences have ideal arithmetic auto-correlations, whose values are zero. However, this is not true for non-binary $ \ell $-sequences.In this work, we develop a trick to determine the arithmetic auto-correlations of $ N $-ary $ \ell $-sequences for $ N>2 $ based on the connection integer $ p^r $ for an odd prime $ p $ and $ r\geq 1 $. The exact values and upper bounds are obtained. The contributions refine and improve Goresky and Klapper's results.We also prove a result on the symmetry of the arithmetic auto-correlation for any $ N $-ary periodic sequences, which extends Hofer and Winterhof's proposition on binary sequences.

title: mimeo: Compiling Public Expert Corpora into Agent Skills and Testing What Transfers
abstract: Giving an agent a file about a named expert can supply hard-to-find material, produce a recognizable persona, or change what the agent decides. These are different claims. We test each one. mimeo is an open-source tool that finds a person's public work, checks each extracted quotation against the cached source text, and writes a file an agent can load. Eight logged builds averaged 38 model calls; the check rejects 13.2% of extracted quotations. We tested four expert files with one coding-agent harness. Knowledge access was clearest: mimeo answered all 20 obscure, quotation-heavy questions; no closed-book condition answered more than 10. Keyword search (BM25) over the same pages answered 15-17, a gap this sample cannot resolve. Grounding showed one clear benefit: personas written from model memory misstated a documented position on 1-4 of 20 answers under every grader; the plain agent and mimeo never did. Every persona was easy to spot on short open prompts, and adding task material lowered identification by 18-23 points. mimeo was no more identifiable than a from-memory profile. Judgment transfer remained unresolved because both tests hit their ceiling: every condition found 94-97% of the problems planted in engineering tasks and scored 94-100% on 16 new application scenarios. An AI-judged "sounds like the expert" score changed with the judge: two of four preferred answers based on a model's stereotype, while two found no difference on the same text. That is a caution against relying on a single AI judge. The evidence supports mimeo as a compact, inspectable reference on a person, not as a demonstrated transfer of their judgment. Toolkit and expert profiles: https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/mimeo

title: Reactivating Test-Time Scaling for Plane Geometry Problem Solving
abstract: Plane geometry problem (PGP) solving has become a critical benchmark for multimodal reasoning because it requires accurate visual perception and precise multi-step symbolic deduction. Although test-time scaling (TTS) has demonstrated remarkable success in general mathematical reasoning, it fails to scale effectively under the symbolic-program paradigm for plane geometry. We identify two key obstacles: limited reasoning diversity induced by rigid symbolic programs and insufficient explicit visual grounding before symbolic deduction. To address these issues, we propose Multi-Trace Synthesis (MTS), which converts each symbolic program into heterogeneous reasoning traces, including executable Python scripts and CoT-augmented variants. We further propose Perception-Augmented (PA) training, which parses diagrams into structured semantic clauses before deduction, and Consensus-Guided Multi-Trace Ensemble (CG-MTE) for efficient self-adaptive inference. Experiments on three geometry benchmarks show that our method consistently improves PGP-solving across model scales and achieves strong performance against both general-purpose MLLMs and specialized geometry solvers. Under test-time scaling, CG-MTE achieves comparable accuracy to high-budget self-consistency while reducing sampling cost by up to 8x. Code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/Jason8Kang/ReTTS-PGPS.

abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum self-adaptive learning to high-dimensional time series forecasting models, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing to enhance prediction accuracy and efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving large datasets and complex feature representations. We propose a novel "Quantum Adaptive Adjustment" mechanism that dynamically adjusts the learning process based on the characteristics of the time series data, leading to improved model performance. The research focuses on mitigating the limitations of traditional machine learning algorithms in handling high dimensionality and complex patterns, presenting a promising approach for improved forecasting capabilities. The paper details the implementation of the quantum self-adaptive learning process, including the introduction of the adaptive adjustment mechanism and a comprehensive evaluation of its effectiveness through simulations and a benchmark dataset. We conclude with a discussion of the potential impact of this approach on various real-world time series forecasting tasks.

title: Title: Non-Standard Quantum State Representation: Entanglement-Driven Geometry
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of a novel quantum state representation, termed the "Geometry-Aware Entanglement Metric," to provide a deeper understanding of entanglement dynamics. Traditional quantum state representations often lack explicit incorporation of the geometry inherent in the entanglement space, hindering our ability to fully characterize and predict entanglement behavior. We propose a new representation that leverages the curvature of the entanglement space as a key metric, allowing for a more comprehensive analysis of entanglement correlations. The proposed metric, coupled with a refined entanglement analysis technique, offers a potential pathway to unlocking new insights into the fundamental properties of entanglement. This work addresses a long-standing challenge in quantum information theory by introducing a fundamentally different approach to representing and manipulating quantum states.

title: Quantum Topology: A Novel Validation Method for Geometric Transformations
abstract: Quantum topology, a burgeoning field, offers a fundamentally different approach to geometric analysis compared to traditional methods. This paper explores the potential of quantum topology to rigorously validate geometric transformations and models, particularly in the context of quantum systems. We propose a novel algorithm leveraging quantum topological properties to assess the correctness of geometric transformations, providing a robust and potentially transformative validation technique. The core claim is that this algorithm can effectively quantify the fidelity of geometric transformations, offering a pathway towards a more reliable understanding of complex geometric models. This research addresses the limitations of current validation methods and highlights the unique capabilities of quantum topology for this application.

title: Probability Graph Models: An Extended Approach
abstract: Probability Graph Models (PGMs) represent complex systems as graphs of nodes and edges, allowing for the modeling of relationships and dynamics. This paper explores an extended approach to PGMs, focusing on the incorporation of dynamic probability update mechanisms to simulate the behavior of complex systems in response to external events and system changes. The core claim is that this enhanced method provides a more realistic and adaptable framework for modeling dynamic systems. The paper introduces the concept of "event-driven probability update," a novel technique for generating probabilistic responses to changing conditions. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a simulation of a simplified system exhibiting emergent behavior. The resulting model exhibits a significant improvement in its ability to capture dynamic system behavior compared to traditional PGMs.
